item.title: Invariance in half-space last passage percolation and directed polymers
item.description: arXiv:2610.37694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove various invariance properties for half-space geometric and exponential last passage percolation and the half-space log-gamma polymer, analogous to the full-space invariances proved by Dauvergne. We use the RSK and geometric RSK correspondences to establish a conditional distributional identity between the half-space models and the corresponding full-space models, which allows us to directly transfer the invariance results in the full space to the half space.
item.dc:creator: Yunhao Lou

item.title: Spine extremality and its frequency in critical branching random walks
item.description: arXiv:2610.37714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the generations at which the distinguished spine of a critical branching random walk occupies the spatial minimum. Under finite positive offspring variance and any nonconstant law of independent real edge increments, their number up to generation $N$ is $(\log N)^{1+o(1)}$ almost surely and has order $\log N$ in probability, with ties included. The same conclusions hold for the unique-minimum event. No spatial moment assumption is needed. The proof combines counting estimates from the spine decomposition with uniform control of extremal multiplicity in an ordinary surviving tree. For a selected minimizer, its one-time probability is the ordinary survival probability $q_n$, and recurrence is equivalent to $\sum_nq_n=\infty$. We also exhibit a critical infinite-variance offspring family for which the weak-minimum event occurs only finitely often, for every nonconstant increment law. We determine the polynomial order of its last occurrence and, for Gaussian or Laplace increments, prove quantitative eventual separation of the spine from the minimum. The sharp frequency constant and limiting distribution in the nonconstant finite-variance model remain undetermined.
item.dc:creator: Haoming Zhang

item.title: Local-to-Global Theorems Based on Cones with Applications to Graph Coloring
item.description: arXiv:2610.37721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local-to-Global theorems are a cornerstone of many of recent developments in theoretical computer science from coding theory and PCPs all the way to analyzing mixing time of Markov chains. Building on trickledown theorems on simplicial complexes, several techniques have been established to obtain tighter local-to-global theorems to analyze the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics, namely matrix trickledown, ${\mathcal C}$-Lorentzian polynomials and more recently Bochner type inequalities. In this paper, we adopt non-local local-to-global/Bochner type inequalities on "cones", corresponding to the local neighborhood of a given vertex, to show that the Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time to sample proper colorings of maximum degree $\Delta$ graphs as long as $q\geq 1.7408\Delta$.
item.dc:creator: Anqi Li, Shayan Oveis Gharan

item.title: The NWU ageing property of the gamma-gamma distribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.37725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Baricz et al. [BPV2011] posed the question of whether the $K$-distribution (or gamma-gamma distribution) satisfies the ageing property known as the new is better than used (NBU) property. In this paper we address this question by establishing that, under certain parameter conditions, the gamma-gamma distribution satisfies the new is worse than used (NWU) property rather than the NBU property. For the remaining parameter ranges, we show that the gamma-gamma distribution is neither NBU nor NWU. The proofs rely on tools from the theory of stochastic orders of random variables. Moreover, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the $K$-distribution is actually the product of two independent gamma random variables, we obtain alternative proofs of our results. Similarly, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the beta-prime distribution is actually the quotient of two independent gamma random variables, we establish analogous NBU/NWU properties for this distribution. We also establish sufficient conditions under which the product of two independent positive random variables possesses the NWU and decreasing failure rate (DFR) properties. On the other hand, we show that the survival function of the $K$-distribution is hyperbolically completely monotone by representing it as the Laplace transform of a random variable belonging to the class of generalized gamma convolutions. As a consequence, we establish some monotonicity properties of the Mills ratio and hazard rate function of the $K$-distribution. These results provide further insight into the ageing and monotonicity properties of the gamma-gamma distribution. In addition, we derive a new integral representation and two new series representations, as well as bounds, for the survival function of the $K$-distribution.
item.dc:creator: \'Arp\'ad Baricz, Dhivya Prabhu K., Snehalata Sahoo, Sanjeev Singh

item.title: Stable limits for the clone-mutant chain with mother-dependent mutation
item.description: arXiv:2610.37815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the general mother-dependent neutral mutation model defined in Blancas, Fittipaldi and Hern\'andez-Torres (2026), consisting of a multitype branching process in which every individual carries one of $d$ alleles and each mutant child acquires a type different from that of its mother, according to a prescribed distribution. We assume that the total offspring distribution is critical and belongs to the domain of attraction of an $\alpha$-stable law, with $\alpha\in(1,2)$, while mutations are rare. Extending the results of Blancas and Rivero (2018), we prove the finite-dimensional convergence of the rescaled Markov chain that records, in each allelic generation, the sizes of the type-specific clone subfamilies and the mutant populations they produce. The limiting clone masses form a multitype Ji\v{r}ina process driven by stable subordinators with drift, whose branching mechanism combines the stable reproduction law with the mother-dependent mutation matrix.
item.dc:creator: Airam Blancas, Mar\'ia Clara Fittipaldi

item.title: Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals: Absorption Probabilities and Conic Intrinsic Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2610.37911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process in $\mathbb R^d$ whose coordinate processes $(U_t^{(i)})_{t\in\mathbb R}$, $1\le i\le d$, are independent, centered, and have covariance function $\mathbb E [U_s^{(i)}U_t^{(i)}]=e^{-|t-s|/2}$. For every $T>0$, we obtain an explicit formula for the probability that the convex hull $\mathrm{conv}\{U_t:0\le t\le T\}$ contains the origin. We obtain a similar formula for a circular Ornstein--Uhlenbeck loop whose covariance is the normalized $T$-periodization of this kernel. For each fixed dimension $d$, we determine the precise long-time asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities, which decay as explicit constants times $T^{d-1} e^{-T/2}$ as $T\to\infty$. We also show that, as $d\to\infty$, the absorption probabilities in both models undergo a transition from $0$ to $1$ around $T=2d$, with a common Gaussian limiting profile on the scale $\sqrt d$. We also obtain explicit formulas for the probability that $\sigma Z$ belongs to the convex hull of Brownian motion or Brownian bridge on $[0,1]$ in $\mathbb R^d$, where $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian vector and $\sigma\ge0$. The large-$\sigma$ asymptotics recover the known formulas for the expected volumes of these convex hulls. Finally, we compute the conic intrinsic volumes of the closed positive hulls of deterministic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals and their circular analogues in Hilbert spaces. Their Grassmann angles coincide with the corresponding Ornstein--Uhlenbeck absorption probabilities. After suitable rescaling, the small-time limits of these conic intrinsic volumes recover the formulas of Gao--Vitale and Gao for the intrinsic volumes of the Brownian body and its Brownian-bridge analogue.
item.dc:creator: Zakhar Kabluchko

item.title: Regularizing the Navier-Stokes Equations via Additive Type Noise plus Small Linear Multiplicative Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.38018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a series of ``regularization by noise in high probability" results for incompressible Navier-Stokes equations $(d\geq3)$, via a new mechanism based on fixed point argument: For initial values in critical Besov space $\dot{B}_{q,\infty}^{-1+d/q}~ (1\leq q<\infty)$, we can expect unique global solutions with $C_{w^*,loc}\big([0,\infty);\dot{B}_{q,\infty}^{-1+d/q}\big)$-paths in high probability if the equations are perturbed by well-constructed additive type noise; for initial values in the ``end-point space" $\dot{B}_{\infty,\infty}^{-1}$ where the equations are locally ill-posed in deterministic setting \cite{BP08}, we can still expect unique solutions on $[0,T]$ (with ``modified" $*$-weak continuous paths) in high probability for large enough $T>0$, if the equations are perturbed by a well-constructed additive type noise plus a ``small" linear multiplicative noise. This means that the regularizing effect can be strengthen by small additional linear multiplicative noise in the sense that the Picard iteration remains effective for values in the largest critical space $\dot{B}_{\infty,\infty}^{-1}$. This work has nothing to do with AI models.
item.dc:creator: Weiquan Chen

item.title: Graph-diameter criteria and sharp dissipation in discrete Wasserstein-Fisher geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.38129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the probability simplex of a finite connected weighted graph with an Onsager operator combining logarithmic-mean transport and mass-conserving Fisher reaction. For every fixed positive reaction parameter, we prove that the entropy Hessian has a finite global lower bound if and only if the original transport graph has diameter at most two. Near a boundary probability, the corresponding criterion is that its positive support reaches every vertex in at most two steps. The proof controls all potential directions under arbitrary multiscale boundary degeneration. For graphs of diameter at most two, the optimal lower bound is Lipschitz on bounded parameter intervals, including the pure-transport endpoint. We also determine the largest instantaneous logarithmic-amplitude dissipation function depending only on the graph and the current amplitude, and construct two-level probabilities attaining it. Its positivity has the same two-step criterion. As consequences, we obtain graph-dependent entropy-decay estimates and exact projective contraction bounds without assuming nonnegative entropic curvature.
item.dc:creator: Rubin Zhang, Ning Zhang

item.title: Two-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is trivial that $1$-dimensional $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates. Coupier, Henry, Jahnel and K\"oppl proved the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in dimension 2; and then for sufficiently large dimensions, B\"aumler, Jahnel, K\"oppl, Lodewijks, Reeves and T\'obi\'as showed this is still true. In this paper, we verify that the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions $d\ge 3.$
item.dc:creator: Jing Liu, Kainan Xiang, Lang Zou

item.title: Strong approximations for dependent random fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.38202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish strong Gaussian approximations for centered stationary random fields on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge2$, represented as measurable functions of i.i.d.\ innovations. Under finite $p$th moments, $p>2$, and sufficiently fast decay of spatial dependence, we construct a single coupling of the field with an i.i.d.\ Gaussian field. Its partial sums, scaled by the long-run standard deviation, approximate those of the original field almost surely, uniformly over all rectangular prefixes and all observation scales. Over a cube of side length $n$, the approximation error is $O_{\mathrm{a.s.}}(n^{\max\{d/p,(d-1)/2\}})$ up to logarithmic factors. While $d/p$ is the familiar moment term, the surface term $(d-1)/2$, absent for independent planar arrays, emerges as a cost of dependence, and cannot be removed even for finite-range Gaussian fields. The assumptions accommodate nonlinear and noncausal fields without imposing mixing. The proof combines a permanent dyadic blocking, a local Gaussian coupling in tensor Haar coordinates driven by a Doob martingale with vanishing conditional third moments, and a comparison of the resulting dependent Gaussian blocks with white noise.
item.dc:creator: Soham Bonnerjee, Sayar Karmakar

item.title: Langevin Dynamics of Non-reciprocally Coupled Spherical Spin Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.38230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the limiting dynamics of two copies of a disordered mean-field spherical $p$-spin system coupled non-reciprocally to one another and initialized independently of the disorder. We prove that, on every finite time interval, as the system size tends to infinity, the empirical correlation and integrated response functions converge almost surely and in $L^q$ for $q \geq 1$, uniformly in time, to the unique non-random solution of a system of coupled integro-differential equations. For even $p$-spin models, we establish stationarity and exponential decay of the correlation and response functions in the high-temperature regime. In the special case of the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, we derive explicit representations of the limiting correlation and integrated response functions. These representations allow us to characterize the long-time dynamics throughout the full range of temperatures. In particular, we prove the occurrence of aging in the low-temperature regime and fluctuation-dissipation behavior in the high-temperature regime, and provide a separate characterization of the dynamics at the critical temperature.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Auffinger, Ratul Biswas

item.title: The Characteristics of Finite Projections of Certain Stochastic Processes and Queues
item.description: arXiv:2610.38339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This thesis studies finite projections of transient regenerative processes, constructed by conditioning regeneration cycles to be finite. It develops comparisons between the original and projected laws, including finite-time bounds and best-approximation properties for specified metrics and comparison classes. Applications concern birth-and-death processes, Markov chains and semi-Markov processes, with explicit queueing examples. Structural results describe projections associated with different regeneration states, invariant measures and connections with Martin boundary kernels. The thesis also studies reconstruction of birth-and-death rates from passage-time laws and continued-fraction representations of Laplace-Stieltjes transforms for skip-free semi-Markov processes, together with truncation-error bounds. This is a corrected English edition of a Romanian doctoral thesis completed in 1998 and defended in 1999. The preface distinguishes the historical work from corrections and later additions made for this edition.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Hlibiciuc

item.title: Phase-Space Realization of Stochastic Multivalued Dynamics with Gyroscopic Subdifferential Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.38381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new framework for stochastic variational inequalities with oblique reflections generated by non-symmetric matrix coefficients. The loss of symmetry fundamentally changes the structure of the reflected dynamics: besides the dissipative component, it produces a genuinely gyroscopic component describing rotational effects that are invisible to the associated energy forms. To capture this hidden component, we consider planar obstacle problems and we lift the dynamics to an extended phase-space system, where the dissipative and gyroscopic mechanisms are naturally separated. This leads to a new notion of solution, for which we establish existence and uniqueness. The resulting framework allows for genuinely rotated reflections, which can lead to angle-controlled rotations.
item.dc:creator: Ioana Ciotir, Andreea Negrut-Grajdeanu, Dan Goreac, Eduard Rotenstein

item.title: On loop-soup clusters in three dimensions and higher
item.description: arXiv:2610.38510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study clusters of the Brownian loop soup on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and of random walk and metric-graph loop soups on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ within a unified framework. For the continuum model, when the one-arm exponent $\xi(\alpha)$ is positive, we prove that almost surely every cluster has Hausdorff dimension $3-\xi(\alpha)$. A key step is to show that, conditioned on the one-arm event, a crossing cluster has capacity comparable to the crossing scale with uniformly positive probability. This gives one-arm estimates of order $\alpha r^{-\xi(\alpha)}$, uniformly down to zero intensity, and shows that $\xi(\alpha)$ is strictly decreasing and left-continuous. Moreover, $1-\xi(\alpha)\asymp\alpha$ as $\alpha\downarrow0$. As another application of the one-arm estimates, we prove that several critical values coincide, resolving a conjecture of Jego and Lupu in arXiv:2601.04840. The proof combines a decoupling technique with a multiscale recursive argument to control the combined effects of large and small loops. These methods also extend to loop soups on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ for $d=3,4,5$, yielding capacity lower bounds of order $r$, $r^2/\log r$, and $r^2$ for the cluster of the origin, conditioned on the one-arm event, throughout the small-loop decay regime. In particular, these bounds imply strict polynomial comparisons between one-arm probabilities at different intensities in dimension three. We also show that the small-loop decay regime on $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ has upper endpoint $\frac{1}{2}$ by adapting the OSSS sharpness framework to the truncated loop soup.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Gao

item.title: The smallest singular value of products of random combinatorial and deterministic matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.38588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p\in(0,1/2]$ be fixed, and let $d,n$ be positive integers satisfying $d=pn$. Let $Q_n$ be an $n\times n$ random combinatorial matrix whose rows are independent and uniformly distributed over the vectors in $\{0,1\}^n$ having exactly $d$ ones. For an arbitrary deterministic invertible $n\times n$ matrix $M$, we establish two-sided bounds for the smallest singular value of $Q_nM$. More precisely, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left( \varepsilon\le s_n(Q_nM)\cdot \|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}} \le \varepsilon^{-2} \right) \ge 1-C\left( \varepsilon+d^{-1/2}+e^{-c\,\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})} \right)-2e^{-cn}, \] where positive constants $C, c$ depend only on $p$ and $\operatorname{sr}$ denotes the stable rank. Consequently, for any sequence of deterministic invertible matrices $M$ satisfying $\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})\to\infty$, $s_n(Q_nM)$ is typically of order $\|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{-1}$. In particular, taking $M=\mathbf I_n$ recovers the known $n^{-1/2}$ scale for $s_n(Q_n)$.
item.dc:creator: Yuxiao Shi, Kexin Yu, Tingzhou Yu

item.title: Finite-State Time-Inhomogeneous Markov Chains Conditioned to Survive
item.description: arXiv:2610.38590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study conditioning on long survival for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains on finite state spaces. We assume that a sequence of substochastic transition kernels converges to an irreducible substochastic kernel and that the transition probabilities admit asymptotic expansions up to order $n^{-2}$. Under these assumptions, we construct a positive space-time harmonic function and prove that the limiting path distributions under conditioning on long survival are given by the corresponding Doob h-transform. We also investigate the long-time behavior of the resulting conditioned process. Finally, we apply our general theory to an elephant random walk, a generalized P\'{o}lya urn model, time-inhomogeneous Wright--Fisher and Moran models, and noncolliding random walks.
item.dc:creator: Kohki Iba

item.title: The Polynomially Self-repelling Motion
item.description: arXiv:2610.38591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: [Kosygina et al. 2023] showed that the rescaled polynomially self-repelling walk does not converge to any Brownian motion perturbed at extrema (BMPE). Motivated by this result, we introduce an explicit candidate for the scaling limit, the polynomially self-repelling motion (PSRM), and study its properties. The construction relies on a new family of continuous stochastic flows, called polynomially self-repelling flows, introduced in [Yu 2026]. A key ingredient in relating the limiting process of the rescaled walk to the PSRM is a joint Ray-Knight theorem for rescaled local time processes, extending the classical Ray-Knight theorems of [T\'oth 1996].
item.dc:creator: Yaolin Yu

item.title: Inhomogeneous Geometric Last Passage Percolation and the $q$-deformed Jacobi Unitary Ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2610.38646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study directed last passage percolation with geometric weights in a spatially inhomogeneous environment. We derive an explicit limit shape and establish fluctuation limits for the passage time, showing that, depending on the strength of the inhomogeneity, the limiting fluctuations are governed by Fredholm determinants associated with either the Airy or Bessel kernel. Our approach is based on an exact relation between the passage time and the smallest particle of the $q$-deformed Jacobi unitary ensemble ($q$-JUE). As part of our analysis, we derive the macroscopic limiting density of the $q$-JUE, which provides a natural $q$-deformation of the classical Wachter distribution, as well as of the limiting distribution of the Meixner ensemble. We further establish Airy and Bessel scaling limits for the smallest particle, which are of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Sung-Soo Byun, Yeong-Gwang Jung, Nick Simm

item.title: The Birthday Problem and the Birthday Person Problem: Intuition, Probability and Cryptographic Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.38749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The present work discusses the birthday problem and the birthday person problem, two classical problems in probability theory widely used to illustrate situations in which human intuition diverges from mathematical results. Taking the work of [1] as its main reference, the study analyzes the probability of birthday coincidences within groups of people, considering a year with 365 days and assuming that all birth dates are equally likely. The birthday problem seeks to determine the probability that at least two people in a group share the same birthday, showing that, even in relatively small groups, the probability of a coincidence increases rapidly due to the large number of possible pairwise comparisons among individuals. In contrast, the birthday person problem investigates the probability that a previously selected person shares the same birthday as another member of the group. This probability increases more slowly, since the number of relevant comparisons is restricted to the pairs formed by the selected person and the remaining members of the group. Despite the interpretative differences, both problems share a similar mathematical foundation based on combinatorial analysis and probability theory. In addition to the theoretical development, numerical results and graphical representations are presented to illustrate the behavior of the probabilities involved and to visualize how the likelihood of coincidences increases as the number of people grows. Finally, applications related to computing and cryptography are discussed, particularly the study of collisions in hash functions and the so-called birthday attack. The discussion highlights the importance of probabilistic reasoning in understanding apparently unlikely phenomena, while also emphasizing how the growth in the number of possible combinations directly influences the results obtained.
item.dc:creator: Alisson Garcia da Silva, Iarythssa Duarte de Ara\'ujo, Francisco M\'arcio Barboza

item.title: Small-time Wasserstein action for KPZ and $\Phi^4_3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the leading small-time Wasserstein action of the full spatial laws of centered KPZ and dynamical $\Phi^4_3$, both started from zero. The leading term is Gaussian, with an explicit heat-trace constant. A common comparison also determines the ratio of length to displacement. For KPZ, a first-chaos cancellation yields a quadratic coupling error. For $\Phi^4_3$, two weighted entropies and an adjoint estimate give comparison bounds uniform in the spectral cutoff. Integrating a Gaussian rotation gives a differentiable realization of the full law; the comparison holds at every positive time.
item.dc:creator: Obayda Julien Assaad

item.title: Universality in randomly connected neural networks: old and new on a conjecture of Geman and Hwang
item.description: arXiv:2610.38893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Randomly connected networks are ubiquitous in computer science, physics or biology. A central question is whether, and how, their collective dynamics depend on the choice of the distribution of the random couplings. Forty years ago, Geman and Hwang formulated a precise version of this \emph{universality} question for randomly connected neural networks. We come back to these conjectures, review what was proven since, provide a few new extensions and propose new conjectures in this paper. For $n$ neuron networks with couplings with a mean scaling as $1/n$ and light enough tails, two classes of limits are expected. For \emph{weakly heterogeneous} couplings, with variance $o(1/n)$, the network is predicted to converge to a McKean--Vlasov equation, and a broad literature has established this under general assumptions. For \emph{strongly heterogeneous} couplings, with variance of order $1/n$, the limit is a non-Markovian equation driven by a self-consistent Gaussian process. After landmark results for Gaussian couplings, universality was only recently established for linear interactions, while the continuous-time nonlinear case relevant to neuroscience remained open. Here, in the weakly heterogeneous regime, we prove quenched convergence on every time interval under a fourth-moment assumption only, and convergence in probability under an assumption slightly stronger than a second moment. In the strongly heterogeneous regime, we prove convergence for nonlinear interactions in continuous time, averaged over sub-Gaussian couplings and on every time interval, by a relative-entropy comparison with Gaussian couplings. We then extend the conjecture to heavy-tailed couplings, and propose a limit driven by a self-consistent $\alpha$-stable process, for which we prove existence for every $\alpha\in(0,2)$ and uniqueness for $\alpha\in[1,2)$, and provide extensive numerical evidence in all three cases.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Touboul

item.title: Proof of the conjecture about inequality of $1/H$-variations of fractional Brownian motion along the equidistant and the Lebesgue partitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an analytic proof of the comparison conjectured by Das, \L{}ochowski, Matsuda and Perkowski for the fractional Brownian level-crossing constant: for standard fractional Brownian motion, $c_H>\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $0<H<1/2$ and $c_H<\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $1/2<H<1$, where $Z\sim N(0,1)$. At $H=1/2$, both constants equal one. The main tool is Gaussian comparison under ordering of increment variances. It applies because truncated variation is translation invariant and lattice-submodular, as follows from its minimum-total-variation characterization. A tangent variogram produces Brownian motion with an independent Gaussian drift on the upper side, and a periodic Brownian bridge on the lower side. The former has an explicit stationary reflection rate. For the latter we calculate an integrated cyclic crossing count by first-passage Laplace transforms. Elementary hyperbolic, theta-series, and Gamma inequalities then give strict comparisons on both full parameter ranges. No numerical integration, simulation, interval certificate, or quantitative local expansion at $H=1/2$ is used.
item.dc:creator: W. M. Bednorz, R. M. {\L}ochowski

item.title: Finite-size ignition laws near a vanishing branching deficit on near-regular simple graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.38912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study heterogeneous bootstrap percolation on uniform simple graphs with prescribed degrees of mean $d\to\infty$ and deviations at most $C\sqrt d$. Thresholds are independently one with probability $(1-c/d)/d$ and two otherwise; seeds form an independent uniform set of prescribed size $a$. Let $T_a$ be the terminal number of active vertices and $b$ be one minus the mean number of threshold-one descendants of a reached vertex. Let $K\sim d^2$ be the quadratic response coefficient. If $b>0$ and $nb^3/K\to\infty$, we prove, uniformly over seed counts $a$, $ \mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)=\Phi(\frac{a-n\alpha_{\mathrm{det}}}{w})+o(1)$ with $w=\sqrt{nb/K}$, where $\alpha_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the exact empirical response-barrier center and $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. Put $a_0=(n/K)^{1/3}$. If $d^4/n\to0$, $a/a_0\to x>0$ and $\lambda=ba_0\to\ell\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)\to p(x,\ell)$, the one-sided Brownian parabolic survival probability. A sequential absolute-error law joins these regimes. A graphical counterexample shows that replacing the exact center by its leading term can cause limiting probability error $1/2$. The proof balances adaptive early-exploration transfer against late concentration at a tunable physical horizon, despite exponentially rare simplicity. We also prove quantitative and mesoscopic-seed refinements in explicitly narrower regimes. The only external graph-enumeration input is a stated reduction of McKay--Wormald's estimate; the probabilistic estimates for the cascade argument are proved in the text and appendices.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr Rodionov

item.title: Anchored isoperimetry in percolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.38941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, for any infinite transitive graph $G$, the infinite cluster after supercritical percolation almost surely inherits the anchored isoperimetry of $G$. Moreover, the probability of violating the corresponding isoperimetric inequality decays exponentially in the isoperimetric profile of the host graph. This was previously known only for nonamenable transitive graphs, $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and very recently for transitive graphs of polynomial growth. Our proof combines the thinning-and-sprinkling technique with a novel counting algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Sahar Diskin, Lyuben Lichev, Ritvik Ramanan Radhakrishnan, Benny Sudakov, Laury Verhoeven

item.title: Dice enterprises and polynomial approximation: uniform query tails
item.description: arXiv:2610.38964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A binary-output dice enterprise uses independent rolls of a die with unknown face probabilities $\mathbf p$ (along with fair coin flips) to simulate a coin with bias $f(\mathbf p)$. We determine which power-law tails, uniform over the closed probability simplex, are attainable for the number $N$ of rolls. For continuous $f$ with values in $(0,1)$ and $q>0$, some enterprise for $f$ satisfies $\sup_{\mathbf p}\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf p}(N>n)=O(n^{-q})$ if and only if $f$ can be approximated uniformly by polynomials of degree $k$ with error $O(k^{-2q})$. When this holds, the same tail bound is attained by an oblivious enterprise, which chooses its number of rolls before rolling. The characterization extends to multiple dice, with total degree on a product of simplices; it then suffices to roll the dice in a fixed cyclic order. For $q>1$, these enterprises have a uniformly bounded expected number of rolls.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Taylor

item.title: Hydrodynamic and Dynamical Phi^4 Limits of Ising-Kac Models with Diffusion-Based Interactions on the Sierpi\'nski Gasket
item.description: arXiv:2610.38982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a general form of Ising--Kac interactions through heat-kernel averaging, with the heat-time parameter replacing the role of the interaction range. From the viewpoint of Dirichlet forms theory, this construction provides an intrinsic analogue of the mesoscopic averaging in classical Kac models when translation invariance is unavailable. We then investigate limits of this model on graph approximations of the Sierpi\'nski gasket. For the associated Glauber dynamics, we establish a hierarchy of scaling limits for the magnetization field. First, at fixed interaction heat time and inverse temperature, we derive a nonlocal hydrodynamic equation on the continuum gasket. Second, as the heat time vanishes and the inverse temperature approaches its mean-field critical value, suitably rescaled hydrodynamic solutions converge to the solution of the deterministic Allen--Cahn equation. Finally, under a joint scaling of graph refinement, interaction heat time, and inverse temperature near criticality, we prove convergence of critical magnetization fluctuations to the solution of the dynamical $\Phi^4$ equation. These results provide a concrete realization of the Ising-$\Phi^4$ correspondence in a geometric setting with non-integer spectral dimension.
item.dc:creator: Hongyi Chen, Seoyeon Yang

item.title: Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.39033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces. The foremost class of examples is provided by group actions with contracting elements, which encompasses, among others, actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and mapping class group actions on Teichm\"uller spaces. We further establish large deviation principles for quasimorphisms on countable groups, and for random walks generated by compositions of Euclidean isometries; also, we discuss extensions and streamlining of known large deviation results for singular values of random matrix products. Finally, in all the contemplated cases, we investigate the analytic properties of the rate function, leveraging its expression as the Fenchel-Legendre transform of a pressure function for certain nonadditive sequences of potentials on shift spaces.
item.dc:creator: Emilio Corso

item.title: An Autonomous Spectral Representation for Fully Asymmetric Spherical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.39115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the large size dynamics of a fully asymmetric spherical Sherrington- Kirkpatrick model, allowing for a distinguished random signal that interacts with the evolving spin configuration. We first derive the large-N dynamical mean-field limit and characterize the law of a typical coordinate by an effective Gaussian process whose covariance must satisfy a self-consistency relation. The resulting formulation is intrinsically nonlocal in time and is not, in its usual form, a closed finite-dimensional dynamical system. Our main contribution is an autonomous spectral representation of this limiting dynamics. We introduce an auxiliary stationary chain of Gaussian replicas whose one-step marginal reproduces the effective field appearing in the dynamical mean- field equation. Applying a matrix-valued Herglotz representation, or equivalently Fourier analysis in the replica index, converts the covariance structure of the chain into a family of finite-dimensional matrix-valued evolution equations indexed by the unit circle. The macroscopic observables, including the signal overlap, are then recovered from explicit spectral integrals. This representation replaces the original two-time self-consistency problem by an autonomous spectral closure and provides a convenient framework for both analysis and numerical computation. We prove the validity of the representation and compare its predictions with direct simulations of the finite-dimensional system
item.dc:creator: James MacLaurin, Pedro Vilanova

item.title: Well-posedness of Rough Differential Equations at the Krylov-R\"ockner Integrability Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.39153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study rough differential equations (RDEs) driven by Brownian (It\^o) rough paths with uniformly locally integrable drifts. The diffusion coefficient is assumed to be uniformly elliptic, of class $C^{2+}$ in space and of bounded variation in time, while the drift is $q$-integrable in time and $p$-integrable in space, uniformly on balls of a fixed radius, for some $p,q$ satisfying the Krylov--R\"ockner condition $\frac dp+\frac2q<1$. We show that, for almost every realization of the It\^o rough path lift of the Brownian motion, such an RDE has a unique solution for every initial value. In other words, for almost every realization of the It\^o lift, the corresponding rough differential equation has exactly one solution in the class of Davie-type solutions, for every initial value; this is the appropriate notion of path-by-path uniqueness for the corresponding stochastic differential equation (SDE) with multiplicative noise. The proof follows the strategy of Shaposhnikov (2016). The principal new ingredients are the stability of RDEs with bounded variation perturbation and Davie-type estimates for the flow of the driftless equation with non-constant diffusion coefficients, which we derive from known maximal regularity estimates for the corresponding parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs).
item.dc:creator: Zimo Hao, Khoa L\^e

item.title: Bregman projections and partition design for accelerating finite Markov chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.39239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Gibbs averaging of finite Markov chains with a prescribed stationary distribution $\pi$. Given a transition matrix $P$ and the Gibbs kernel $G$ induced by a state-space partition, we prove that $GPG$ is an information projection for every admissible Bregman generator $\phi$, with divergences defined using transition probabilities relative to $\pi$. A Pythagorean identity characterizes this projection and recovers the relative entropy and weighted Frobenius cases. A dual characterization identifies $GPG$ as a kernel closest to stationarity among those with the same projection chain as $P$; for relative entropy, it maximizes the entropy rate. The identities also give monotonicity under partition coarsening. For every reversible ergodic baseline $P$, Gibbs averaging cannot increase the squared weighted Frobenius distance to stationarity at any positive integer time, and the inequality is strict unless $P=GPG$. The corresponding mixing time therefore cannot increase. To choose the partition, we identify the divergence of $G$ from stationarity as the exact worst-case divergence of $GPG$ over all $\pi$-stationary baselines $P$. This objective depends only on the block masses. We give an exact algorithm for concave block costs, including those arising from relative entropy and power generators $\phi(u)=u^p$ with $1<p<2$, and a greedy approximation algorithm with a provable guarantee for $p>2$. For power generators $\phi(u)=u^p$ with $p>1$, the objective is proportional to Tsallis entropy of order $2-p$: its minimization favors imbalanced block masses when $1<p<2$ and balanced block masses when $p>2$, while all $k$-block partitions have the same objective value when $p=2$. A numerical experiment compares the resulting projected chains with a local Metropolis sampler on a multi-modal $\pi$.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. H. Choi, Youjia Wang

item.title: Bounding martingale dimension by spectral dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.39312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the martingale dimension of a broad class of strongly local regular Dirichlet forms is bounded above by a small-scale version of spectral dimension. This resolves a conjecture of Hino for this class of spaces, extending his earlier results beyond self-similar fractals. Our proof uses differentiation of energy measures to select good blow-up scales and construct approximately harmonic coordinates. We then study weak limits of their Euclidean image measures and combine an integration-by-parts argument with uniform Sobolev inequalities to establish the dimension bound.
item.dc:creator: Aobo Chen, Mathav Murugan

item.title: Stopping Rules and the Poisson Boundary of Random Walks on Countable Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.39345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the terminal laws and Poisson boundaries obtained by stopping random walks on countable groups. For a transient walk, we give a direct Green-potential characterization of randomized stopping distributions and show that the terminal law determines the mean stopping time. On free groups, this yields finitely supported randomized stopping distributions at a positive total variation distance from every ordinary stopping distribution. We construct symmetric, fully supported recurrent measures of finite entropy on countable locally finite groups and obtain ordinary strict boundary enlargements when the group is not Choquet-Deny. For generating source and terminal measures of finite entropy, positive asymptotic entropy of the source forces the stopping time to have finite mean. A direct proof of the finite-mean entropy formula and boundary preservation then shows that a finite-entropy stopping chain has at most one strict enlargement. An exact stopped-word entropy identity shows that infinite-mean ordinary stopping with a finite-entropy terminal law has infinite conditional history entropy.
item.dc:creator: Yinghan Zhang

item.title: Optimal fiber comparisons for random tensors
item.description: arXiv:2610.39389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Seginer's matrix norm comparison to tensors with optimal dependence on the tensor order. For a real tensor $T$ of order $k\ge2$ with centered, integrable, independent and identically distributed entries, we prove $\mathbb{E} f(T)\le\mathbb{E}\lVert T\rVert_{\mathrm{inj}} \le C\sqrt{k\log k}\,\mathbb{E} f(T)$, where $f(T)$ is the largest Euclidean norm of a one-dimensional fiber and $C$ is universal. The comparison holds for every finite rectangular format, and the entry law may depend on both the dimensions and the tensor order. We show that the factor $\sqrt{k\log k}$ is optimal by considering Rademacher tensors on $[2]^k$.
item.dc:creator: Ziqian Lin, Huangang Lu

item.title: Exponential singularity and rank bounds for random symmetric matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.39424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ real symmetric random matrix whose entries above the diagonal are independent, each with largest atom at most $\beta\in (0,1)$. The diagonal entries have an arbitrary joint distribution and are independent of the entries above the diagonal. We prove that \[ \mathbb{P}[\mathrm{rank}(A)\le n-k]\le 2e^{-c_\beta nk},\qquad 1\le k\le n, \] where $c_\beta>0$ depends only on $\beta$. This extends Han's corank bound to the full range $1\le k\le n$. No moment assumptions are needed, and the entries need not be centered or identically distributed. In particular, the case $k=1$ gives an exponential singularity bound under the uniform atom assumption. Our argument also gives a new proof of the exponential singularity bound for symmetric Rademacher matrices obtained by Campos, Jenssen, Michelen, and Sahasrabudhe. For every fixed $p\in (0,1)$, it yields the exponential singularity bound conjectured by Costello and Vu for the adjacency matrix of the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$, where the case $p=1/2$ was previously proved by Han.
item.dc:creator: Huaijin Liang, Kexin Yu, Tingzhou Yu

item.title: Exponential Ergodicity and Invariant Distribution of a Degenerate Reflected SDE with Stable Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.39471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a two-dimensional degenerate stochastic differential equation with oblique reflection and spectrally positive strictly stable noise of index in $(1,2)$, motivated by join-the-shortest-queue systems with heavy-tailed interarrival times. A polynomial-exponential Lyapunov function and fixed-time minorization establish positive Harris recurrence and exponential ergodicity in weighted total variation. We construct the invariant law from a stable path and prove its absolute continuity. Regulator identities describe stationary dependence and recover the joint Laplace transform from the queue marginal. Idleness inherits the classical stable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck tail; the queue has a sharp exponential tail with a polynomial prefactor whose power is half the stable index and a positive constant represented through regeneration. Conditional on small idleness, idleness divided by the conditioning threshold and the queue converge to independent beta and size-biased limits. Under large-queue conditioning, normalized idleness and queue excess converge to independent Mittag-Leffler and exponential limits.
item.dc:creator: Guodong Pang, Wei You

item.title: Weighted Harris--oscillation contraction and invariant expectations for nonlinear Markov semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.39492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a weighted contraction principle for sublinear Markov semigroups on noncompact state spaces. Its abstract inputs are a Lyapunov drift condition and a strict local contraction of oscillations on a Lyapunov sublevel set. For locally uniformly parabolic diffusion semigroups, the latter is obtained by applying the parabolic Harnack inequality to both the upper evolution and its conjugate lower evolution: if $u=T_t\varphi$, then $u-m$ and $M-u$ solve the upper and lower Bellman equations, respectively. Combining the resulting local oscillation contraction with the Lyapunov drift yields a strict contraction in a weighted oscillation seminorm, a unique invariant sublinear expectation in the finite-Lyapunov-moment class, and weighted exponential convergence for Borel observables controlled by the Lyapunov function. To treat bounded Borel data for $G$-SDEs, we use a canonical covariance-law representation, progressively measurable state maps compatible with conditioning and pasting, and a stopped dynamic programming principle. A probabilistic Krylov--Safonov argument then gives positive-time H\"older regularisation before viscosity identification, thereby avoiding a measurable-data envelope argument. The abstract result is verified for ordinary locally uniformly elliptic SDEs, multiplicative $G$-SDEs, and the full equation with quadratic-variation drift \[ dX_t=b(X_t)\,dt +\sum_{i,j=1}^m h_{ij}(X_t)\,d\langle B^i,B^j\rangle_t +\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(X_t)\,dB_t^j. \] For the full equation the hypotheses are expressed through the effective drift and covariance and are required uniformly over all covariance scenarios. Finally, the contraction and stochastic continuity of the associated stationary process yield ergodicity in the sense of Feng and Zhao.
item.dc:creator: Danyang Zhao, Huaizhong Zhao

item.title: Local Convergence of Triadic Closures of Sparse Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Triadic closure is a natural mechanism for modeling the clustering phenomenon observed in many real-world networks. Given a possibly random undirected graph $H$, we consider pairs of non-adjacent vertices that have a common neighbor. Conditional on $H$, each such pair is joined by an edge independently and simultaneously, with a probability depending on the degrees of its endpoints and on the number of their common neighbors. The resulting graph is called a triadic closure of $H$. We study the effect of this operation on local convergence. More precisely, we prove that if a sequence of potentially random finite undirected graphs of $\left( H_n \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges locally in probability to a rooted graph $H^*$, then the corresponding sequence of triadic closures converges locally in probability to the same triadic closure of $H^*$. As a consequence, we obtain a general limit theorem for the clustering coefficients of triadic closures. In particular, we show that the triadic closures can have a strictly positive limiting clustering coefficients even when the limiting clustering coefficients of the parent graph sequence is zero. Finally, we apply our results to several classical sparse random graph models including Erd\H{o}s-R\'{e}nyi, configuration, preferential attachment models and compute the limiting clustering coefficients of their triadic closures.
item.dc:creator: Himasish Talukdar

item.title: Ghirlanda-Guerra identities and cavity equations for diluted spin glass models
item.description: arXiv:2610.39542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note supplies the details of the cavity lower bound used in "The M\'ezard-Parisi formula" [8]. Specifically, we show that small perturbations that do not change the limiting free energy can be chosen so that the asymptotic Gibbs measures arising in the Aizenman-Sims-Starr lower bound satisfy both the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities and the cavity equations. These calculations are standard and require only minor modifications of arguments already available in the literature. We record them here for completeness, avoiding a lengthy repetition of these arguments in [8].
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Panchenko

item.title: The M\'ezard-Parisi formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.39545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proves the M\'ezard-Parisi formula for the free energy of random $K$-sat and diluted $p$-spin models with even $p$, completing an approach developed in earlier work of the author and collaborators. The upper bound was established by Franz and Leone. Here the matching lower bound is proved for a general class of diluted models under symmetry and integrability assumptions. The main new contribution is a proof of an approximate form of the M\'ezard-Parisi reproducibility hypothesis without assuming that the overlap distribution has finite support.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Panchenko

item.title: The Berry--Esseen estimate in the Boolean central limit theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.39743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We estimate the L\'evy distance to the symmetric Bernoulli distribution for normalized Boolean convolution powers of a probability measure with mean zero and variance one. If the absolute moment of order $r$ is finite, we obtain the upper bounds $o(n^{-(r-2)/6})$ for $2<r<5$ and $O(n^{-1/2})$ for $r\ge5$. The proof relies on an inequality that controls the L\'evy distance to the Bernoulli law by the values of the reciprocal Cauchy transform at two points. For each $r\ge2$, we also construct a single fixed distribution whose absolute moments are finite exactly up to order $r$, and show that the exponent $\min\{(r-2)/6,1/2\}$ cannot be improved. Under only a finite second moment assumption, the convergence can be arbitrarily slow.
item.dc:creator: Maejima Makoto, Noriyoshi Sakuma

item.title: Functional limit theorems for Galton-Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration towards a deterministic limit function
item.description: arXiv:2610.39771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of a sequence of Galton-Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration when the limit of the means of the offspring distributions is equal to 1. Under a growth condition on the variances of the offspring distributions, assuming the locally uniform convergence of the expectation functions of properly scaled immigration processes towards a c\`adl\`ag function, and the locally uniform convergence of the mean absolute deviation functions of the scaled immigration processes in question towards zero, we establish a functional limit theorem for the sequence of Galton-Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration in question towards a deterministic limit process. We also provide some applications, among others, we show that a recent result of Rahimov and Sharipov (2024) on a functional limit theorem for a sequence of nearly critical Galton-Watson processes with dependent immigration can be recovered using our result.
item.dc:creator: Matyas Barczy, D\'aniel Bezd\'any

item.title: Strong rate for one-dimensional driftless continuous strict local martingales
item.description: arXiv:2610.39896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For one-dimensional strict local martingales of the form $\mathrm{d} X_t=\sigma(X_t) \mathrm{d} W_t$ starting from $X_{0}=x_{0}>0$, we prove the strong rate $\mathbb{E}\left[|X^h_N-X_T|\right] \lesssim h^{\min\{\theta\alpha,\frac{1}{2}\}}$ for a discrete scheme~$X^h$ truncated at a level $h^{-\alpha}$, with time step~$h$, as $h\downarrow 0$, where~$\theta$ depends on the truncation property. For the CEV model $\sigma(x)\equiv x^{1+\gamma}$ in particular, the rate is~$\frac{1}{2}$ for any $\gamma \in (0,1)$ (up to a logarithmic pre-factor at $\gamma=\frac{1}{2}$).
item.dc:creator: Antoine Jacquier

item.title: Interacting particles in random irregular media
item.description: arXiv:2610.39903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we first develop novel tools of independent interest in the field of stochastic calculus related to SDEs with distributional drift, namely the formulation of a quasi-Stroock-Varadhan martingale problem in the sense that the test functions are of class $C^{1,2}$ instead of solutions of Kolmogorov type PDE. This has several applications, among which, the time restriction and the notion of conditional rough martingale problem and related solution.
item.dc:creator: Luca Bondi (UNITO, OC), Elena Issoglio (UNITO), Francesco Russo (ENSTA Paris, OC)

item.title: Lie point symmetry analysis of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model with exponential claim sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.39920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We carry out a Lie point symmetry analysis of the coupled integro-differential system satisfied by the conditional Gerber--Shiu functions of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model. In the model, claim sizes are exponential, the intensity of the next claim arrival depends on whether the current claim exceeds a random threshold, and both the volatility and the premium rate may depend on the surplus. We write the system as the restriction to the half-line of a far-field operator with prescribed exterior data, derive the complete set of determining equations, including the condition imposed by the nonlocal convolution term, and solve them. The resulting group classification holds for every surplus-dependent volatility and premium of the form considered and for every absolutely continuous or constant threshold distribution. A non-trivial symmetry beyond scaling and superposition exists if and only if the volatility and the premium rate are constant, and it is then exactly the translation in the surplus variable. We construct the optimal system of one-dimensional subalgebras. We show that the invariant solutions of the combined translation--scaling generators exist precisely when a $2\times2$ generalized Lundberg determinant vanishes, and we give this determinant for an arbitrary threshold distribution, with explicit forms for the constant and exponential thresholds. We prove existence and sign properties of the adjustment coefficient, derive its sensitivities to all model parameters, and establish Cram\'er--Lundberg-type asymptotics for the Gerber--Shiu functions, including the limit of the ratio between the two regimes. A numerical study shows that claim-size-driven dependence lowers the adjustment coefficient markedly below that of an independent model with the same mean claim intensity.
item.dc:creator: Aminu Ma'aruf Nass, Kassimu Mpungu, Rahmatullah Ibrahim Nuruddeen, Yaqoob Al Rahbi

item.title: On self-similar random quotients of the line
item.description: arXiv:2610.39953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A surprisingly wide variety of important random fractal metric spaces in modern probability theory can be viewed as self-similar random quotients of the real line, including the continuum random tree, Liouville quantum gravity surfaces, the trace of Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and self-similar ($s=2d$) long-range percolation on $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that the metric and resistance growth dimensions are well-defined in a certain sense for every random metric space in a class containing all of the above examples. Our results are new for the trace of Brownian motion.
item.dc:creator: Johannes B\"aumler, Tom Hutchcroft

item.title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.40067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.
item.dc:creator: Kohki Sakamoto

item.title: A total variation threshold for the first coordinates of uniform parking functions via Lorentzian polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.40082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\pi_n$ be a uniform parking function of size $n$. We determine the scale at which its first $k$ coordinates cease to be close in total variation to $k$ independent uniform variables on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The distance is comparable to $1\wedge \sqrt{k\log(k+1)/n}$, uniformly for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and tends to one above the scale $n/\log n$. At the critical scale $k\sim\lambda n/\log n$, it converges to $2\Phi(\sqrt{\lambda/\pi})-1$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. A key ingredient is the Lorentzian property of the occupation generating polynomial of parking functions. Together with a strengthened Han inequality, this yields a relative entropy estimate for approximation by the product of the one-coordinate marginals.
item.dc:creator: Igor Kortchemski

item.title: Multi-excited random walks on general trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.40084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study multi-excited random walks on infinite locally finite trees. The model is described by placing a stack of ``cookies'' at each vertex, with one cookie consumed on each successive visit. As long as cookies remain, the walk is in an excited regime and makes nearest-neighbour steps according to a prescribed sequence of biases. Once the stack is exhausted, the walk is in a non-excited regime and moves uniformly among the neighbouring vertices. The model is closely connected to foraging ecology, where repeated visits to a location can deplete local resources and thereby influence the attractiveness of that location for future visits. We prove that the process exhibits a sharp phase transition between recurrence and transience. The critical threshold is determined by the branching-ruin number of the tree, which is equal to the Hausdorff dimension of the tree's boundary under a suitable metric. Our result substantially extends Zerner's recurrence-transience criterion for multi-excited random walks on $\mathbb Z$ [Probab. Theory Related Fields 133 (2005)] to general trees.
item.dc:creator: Jack Mills, Tuan-Minh Nguyen

item.title: Ergodicity for the Two-Dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations with Shear-Thickening Viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2610.40086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. After the problem is formulated as an abstract stochastic evolution equation on suitable function spaces, the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions are established through local monotonicity methods. Moment estimates are then obtained and used to prove the existence of an ergodic invariant probability measure via the Krylov-Bogolyubov technique. The uniqueness of the ergodic invariant measure is subsequently established by constructing a generalized coupling through a controlled auxiliary equation. Finally, the results are extended to other types of viscosities as well as to different stochastic hydrodynamical models.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Bunting

item.title: Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits for the total edge-length of random directional nearest-neighbour graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study planar random spatial graphs defined by inserting an edge between every point of a homogeneous Poisson process on the unit square and a nearest-neighbour within a fixed cone of directions (if there is such a point). We prove large-sample distributional limit theorems for the total Euclidean edge length of the graph, where the limit distribution is either Gaussian (due to contributions from the bulk) or, when one or both of the boundaries of the cone of directions align with the edges of the square, a convolution of Gaussian with a non-Gaussian law arising from boundary effects due to long edges near a boundary. This work extends previously known cases, including the ordinary nearest-neighbour graph (full cone of directions), where the Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Bickel & Breiman and Avram & Bertsimas, and Bhatt & Roy's minimal directed spanning forest (with 'south-west' directions), where the non-Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Penrose & Wade.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Georgiou, Qasem M. Tawhari, Andrew Wade

item.title: Packing and covering random trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.40150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the sizes of optimal packings and coverings of conditioned branching processes by balls with growing radii. We find a universal limiting constant, and thereby establish universality of packing and covering numbers across different scales and different offspring distributions. To be precise, for $\mu$ an offspring distribution with mean $1$ and finite variance $\sigma^2$ we let $T_n$ be a Bienaym\'e tree with offspring distribution $\mu$ conditioned to have size $n$. We prove that the packing number (resp. covering number) of $T_n$ with balls of radii $1\ll \gamma_n \ll n^{1/2}$ is asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C} n /(\sigma^2 \gamma_n^2)$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C} n /(4\sigma^2 \gamma_n^2)$), for a universal constant $\mathfrak{C}$. We also show that the order of limits can be exchanged and that the same limit occurs when we first consider the limiting covering number of $T_n$ by balls of fixed radius $R$, and thereafter let $R$ tend to $\infty$. We then extend these results to the Brownian continuum random tree conditioned to have mass $1$. For this model, we prove that the packing (resp. covering) number with balls of radii $\varepsilon$ are asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C}/\varepsilon^2$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C}/(4\varepsilon^2)$), for the same constant $\mathfrak{C}$, in contrast with a conjecture by Aldous. Finally, our results answer a question by Devroye, Eide and Pralat on the asymptotic burning number of mean $1$ finite variance Bienaym\'e trees of size $n$, by showing that it lies between $(c+o(1)) n^{1/3}$ and $(2c+o(1))n^{1/3}$ with high probability, for a constant $c$ that only depends on the offspring variance.
item.dc:creator: Caelan Atamanchuk, Simon Briend, Serte Donderwinkel, Elaine Herrera

item.title: Limiting ESD for a weighted sample covariance matrix
item.description: arXiv:2610.40368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) of the random matrix $M_N=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N f(|\pi Y_i|^2)\,Y_iY_i^\top$, where $\pi$ is a rank $k$ orthogonal projector on $\R^p$, $Y_1,\dots,Y_N$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian vectors, and $k\to \infty$, $p/N\to \gamma$. We here assume that $f(x)=g(x/k)$ for some function $g$ discontinuous at $x=1$. We show that the asymptotic ESD is characterized by a Marchenko--Pastur equation, independently of $k$. We also show that the result extends to sub Gaussian random vectors $Y_i$ and to the case where the projector is replaced with a more general weight $\phi(Y_i)$. Last, in the Gaussian case, we study the emergence of outliers due to the weighting.
item.dc:creator: Sandrine P\'ech\'e

item.title: Exponential Convergence of the Lifted Gradient Flow of the Bass Functional
item.description: arXiv:2610.40404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish multidimensional exponential convergence of the lifted Bass gradient flow in martingale optimal transport. Let $\mu\le_{cx}\nu$ be an irreducible pair, with compact convex target support, source support strictly inside the target support, and target density bounded above and bounded away from zero almost everywhere on its interior. For every bounded $\sigma(X)$-measurable initial state, the flow converges exponentially in $L^2$ to the global minimizer with the prescribed mean, and the functional value gap decays exponentially. Both bounds hold at every nonnegative time with the exact initial errors as prefactors. The quantitative step is strong convexity on sets with a common $L^\infty$ bound and a fixed mean. We prove it by interpolating entropic endpoint potentials, using two conditional copies to cancel the unknown potential increment, and obtaining a Hessian lower bound uniform in the regularization parameter. Removing the regularization yields curvature for the original functional; the known qualitative theory supplies a common bound for the orbit. This extends the one-dimensional exponential-convergence result of Backhoff-Veraguas, Pammer, and Schachermayer. The main result is formalized in Lean 4. AI was used in preparing the paper (see Section 8).
item.dc:creator: Danila Litvinov

item.title: The velocity is deterministic in random walk in 2-valued i.i.d. random environment
item.description: arXiv:2610.40464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the limiting velocity for (nearest-neighbour) random walk in i.i.d. random environment is deterministic when the local environment is supported on two points. No ellipticity is assumed. The proof uses a clever adaption (suggested by ChatGPT) of coupling arguments previously developed by the authors. It extends to i.i.d. environments where the local environments are mixtures of two such points.
item.dc:creator: Mark Holmes, Thomas S. Salisbury

item.title: Mutant invasion in stochastic individual-based models with cyclic resident dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.40466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a resident community oscillates, can a rare mutant invade, and with which probability? We study a multitype birth-and-death process with interactions, in which population sizes are of the order of a carrying capacity $K$, and whose large-population limit, as $K\to\infty$, has a hyperbolically stable limit cycle for the $D-1$ resident types. We introduce a single individual of a new type. We prove that, as long as the mutant population is smaller than $\varepsilon K$ for a small $\varepsilon>0$, the resident population sizes divided by $K$ stay close to a moving point of the cycle, whose asymptotic phase moves by at most $O(\varepsilon)$ per period. We deduce that, for large $K$, the mutant dies out quickly if its growth rate averaged over one period, $f(\bar{\mathbf n})$, is negative, and that it invades with positive probability, in a time close to $\ln K/f(\bar{\mathbf n})$, if $f(\bar{\mathbf n})$ is positive. This justifies a criterion used heuristically in ecology for decades. The invasion probability, unlike $f(\bar{\mathbf n})$, depends on the phase of the cycle at which the mutant arises. We give it explicitly through Kendall's formula, and show that its average over the cycle, weighted by the birth rate of the mutant, equals $f(\bar{\mathbf n})$. In predator-prey, competitive and mutualistic examples, the invasion probability varies by a factor between $2$ and $600$ along the cycle, and individual-based simulations agree quantitatively with the theory. After invasion, the oscillations may vanish, persist on a cycle of higher dimension, or give way to chaotic coexistence.
item.dc:creator: Sylvain Billiard, Chlo\"e Mian, Charline Smadi, Andr\'as T\'obi\'as

item.title: Random Matching Between Distinct Distributions in Two Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given two independent $n$-point samples drawn from possibly distinct probability distributions on a compact 2-dimensional surface, we minimize the total squared distance over all perfect bipartite matchings. Under regularity assumptions, the expected matching cost minus $n$ times the squared 2-Wasserstein distance between the sampling distributions grows logarithmically with $n$. We determine this difference up to an additive $o(1)$ error, including the dependence of the logarithmic coefficient and constant term on geometry and sampling distributions, and establish the existence of a universal constant shared by these formulas. Our analysis expresses the expected matching cost in terms of the cost of transporting a heat-smoothed sample back to its original points. The reductions giving this relation hold in every dimension and for general costs under suitable assumptions, with consequences beyond the setting studied here. In two dimensions, the relation is exact up to an additive $o(1)$ error, so determining the matching cost amounts to evaluating the smoothing cost with the same accuracy. We obtain this evaluation by subdividing the domain and exploiting cancellations between the sample and its own smoothing.
item.dc:creator: Yunzong Xu

item.title: Quantitative sub-ballisticity of self-avoiding walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove quantitative sub-ballisticity for the self-avoiding walk on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$. Namely, we obtain an explicit exponential rate of decay for the probability that a self-avoiding walk of length $n$ reaches distance at least $vn$, in terms of $v>0$. As a consequence, we show that the displacement of an $n$-step self-avoiding walk is at most $n/\exp(c\log^* n)$ with very high probability. Previously, only a non-quantitative $o(n)$ bound was known from the work of Duminil-Copin and Hammond. Along the way, we show that at criticality the partition function of bridges of length $n$ is on average bounded by $C/\log\log n$, which we believe to be of independent interest. Our approach is based on a quantitative analysis of the original nonconstructive proof of Duminil-Copin and Hammond using ideas from proof theory.
item.dc:creator: Ekin Arik\"ok, Christoforos Panagiotis, Nicholas Pischke, Thomas Powell

item.title: Convergence of a drainage network model with branching to the Brownian net
item.description: arXiv:2610.40555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a drainage network model represented by a system of coalescing random walks exhibiting long range dependence before coalescence. This model was introduced by Gangopadhyay et. al. [GRS04] and Coletti et. al. [CFD09] proved its convergence to the Brownian web under diffusive scaling. Santos et. al. [SVZ24] considered a branching version of this model where branching occurs with low probabilities varying with the scaling parameter and showed that any sub-sequential limit contains a copy of the Brownian net. It was conjectured that the limit is indeed the Brownian net. In this work we prove this conjecture. Further, compared to [SVZ24], we explore the question of scaling limit in a wider spectrum of scaling regime. This work contributes to the broader understanding of the basin of attraction of the Brownian net.
item.dc:creator: Krishnamurthi Ravishankar, Kumarjit Saha

item.title: A self-normalized law of the iterated logarithm for Rademacher random multiplicative functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on the squarefree integers, and let $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}f(n)$. We prove a two-sided law of the iterated logarithm normalized by the full predictable quadratic variation \[ Q(x)=\sum_{p\le x}\bigg(\sum_{\substack{m\le x/p\\ P(m)<p}}f(m)\bigg)^2 \] of the martingale obtained by revealing the prime signs. Almost surely, \[ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{M(x)}{\sqrt{2Q(x)\log\log x}}=1, \qquad \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{M(x)}{\sqrt{2Q(x)\log\log x}}=-1. \] The same equalities hold with $\log\log Q(x)$ in the denominator. The almost sure cluster set of the normalized sum is $[-1,1]$. This gives a self-normalized version of the questions of Wintner and Erd\H{o}s on almost sure fluctuations. We also prove that $Q(x)/q(x)$ cannot converge in probability to $1$ for any positive deterministic function $q$. Moreover, \[ \limsup_{x\to\infty} \frac{|M(x)|}{\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4}} \] is either an almost surely finite and positive random variable with nondegenerate distribution or infinite almost surely. We do not determine which alternative holds.
item.dc:creator: Dariusz Buraczewski, Alexander Iksanov

item.title: JT gravity as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks
item.description: arXiv:2610.40645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that flat Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity arises as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks. We give a clean criterion, formulated in terms of branching explorations, for a discrete model to converge to this conjecturally universal limit. For simplicity, we apply this criterion to a Boltzmann ensemble of disks with rectilinear boundary, defined by summing over combinatorial types and integrating over lengths. As the length of a distinguished side tends to infinity, the rescaled surface converges in law to a continuum random surface prescribed by Ferrari's path-integral formulation of JT gravity. Convergence is in the topology of smooth convergence of the conformal factors on compact subsets of the interior when uniformizing in a fixed domain; the limiting conformal factor is described by a harmonic Gaussian field closely related to holomorphic multiplicative chaos. The crux is a branching exploration of flat JT gravity whose lengths evolve as conditioned Cauchy processes and whose unexplored components are conditionally independent. We construct this exploration using a conformal welding theorem proved in a companion paper, and show that it is the scaling limit of Budd's row-by-row exploration of the discrete disks, analogous to the peeling of random planar maps. Under a tightness condition, our criterion upgrades this convergence to a conformal scaling limit for the discrete disks. Other natural combinatorial disk models admit analogous first-row recursions, providing a route to their scaling limits.
item.dc:creator: Morris Ang

item.title: Pooled Testing under Congestion: Operational Scaling Laws for Pool-Size Selection
item.description: arXiv:2610.37729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical pooled-testing rules choose pool sizes to reduce the number of tests. In practice, however, samples arrive over time, pools take time to form, testing capacity is finite, and positive pools create bursts of follow-up work. These operational features can make the test-efficient pool size far from the delay-efficient one. We formulate pooled testing with stochastic arrivals and finite testing capacity as a queueing system, and derive exact performance representations and asymptotic scaling laws for fixed-batch Dorfman testing and a dynamic two-threshold policy. The analysis reveals three distinct design regimes. When test usage is the main concern, the classical Dorfman rule is recovered and the optimal pool size scales with the inverse square root of prevalence. When delay accumulated while the laboratory is busy testing another batch matters, positive pools create service-time variability that grows more rapidly with pool size than the mean retesting burden, and the optimal scale shifts to the inverse cube root of prevalence. When waiting to assemble a pool is itself costly, the optimal fixed pool size remains bounded even as prevalence becomes very small. Under severe capacity scarcity, congestion remains relevant at the classical Dorfman scale: the square-root law survives, but with a capacity-dependent constant. Dynamic pooling separates two operational decisions that fixed pool sizes conflate. A lower threshold determines when routine testing should begin, while an upper threshold limits pooling when backlog is high. The lower threshold follows the cube-root scale, whereas the upper threshold primarily acts as congestion control. The results show how prevalence, capacity, and delay jointly determine pooling decisions and explain why operationally optimal pools can be much smaller than those suggested by test-efficiency calculations alone.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Dimitriou, Johan van Leeuwaarden

item.title: Finite algebras whose equational probability spectrum contains a big gap
item.description: arXiv:2610.37841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the finite algebras $\mathbf{A}$ for which there is no value $p$ satisfying $\frac{1}{|A|}<p<1$ in the equational probability spectrum of $\mathbf{A}$. We will use the classification to determine which finite algebras have minimal equational probability spectrum. In our final section, we explore the relationship, for finite algebras, between the properties of (i)~having a finite equational probability spectrum and (ii)~being an abelian algebra.
item.dc:creator: Carles Card\'{o}, Keith A. Kearnes, \'{A}gnes Szendrei

item.title: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift
item.description: arXiv:2610.37866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study conformal prediction under covariate shift with a known covariate density ratio, seeking prediction sets with minimum expected length under the target distribution. For every calibration sample size, we prove that the rule combining the inverse conditional-density score with randomized weighted conformal calibration minimizes this expected length among all rules valid over the full weighted-exchangeability class. We approximate the oracle using quantile and kernel histograms, including forest-weighted estimators, and select estimators and tuning parameters by resampling to estimate calibrated target length. On a bounded response domain, we bound excess length linearly in $L^1$ density error at fixed calibration size, without requiring a uniform positive lower bound on the true density.
