We also bound selection-pool and resampling errors. Under explicit growth conditions, the selected procedure approaches the same oracle while the calibration size remains fixed. Experiments on 36 known-density configurations and four public regression datasets compare coverage, prediction-set length, and runtime with existing methods. In targeted low-coverage and strong-shift comparisons, inverse-density selection yields shorter mean sets in most cases and lower mean runtime than the evaluated weighted baselines, with some differences in achieved coverage.
item.dc:creator: Zhongyang Li

item.title: Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Semilinear Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.38166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a rigorous mathematical framework for the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations. The invariant Gaussian measure of the associated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, which need not be time-reversible, serves as the reference measure. We define thermodynamic quantities in terms of probability densities and derive the entropy balance equation. We obtain explicit expressions for the entropy production rate and prove that its vanishing in the stationary state is equivalent to time reversibility. Sample-path entropy production is identified with the logarithm of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the forward path measure with respect to the time-reversed path measure and is shown to satisfy fluctuation theorems. For nonstationary systems, sample-path entropy production decomposes into housekeeping heat and free-energy dissipation, each satisfying an integral fluctuation theorem. Both have nonnegative expectations, and the mean free-energy dissipation equals the decrease in relative entropy with respect to the stationary distribution. The theory is applied to semilinear stochastic heat equations with spatially correlated noise, a random polymer model, a nonlinear model with a divergence-free drift, and two coupled stochastic heat equations in contact with heat baths at different temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Zelin Liu, Hao Ge

item.title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part II: Langevin Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.38206v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem on the sphere, in which we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\mathcal{S}_N=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^N:\lVert x\rVert^2=N\}$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. Continuing the program initiated in Part I [arXiv:2610.16705], we show that spherical Langevin dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization. Together with Part I, our results demonstrate that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.
item.dc:creator: Aniket Das, Tselil Schramm

item.title: Data-driven stochastic asymptotic regularization for ill-posed inverse problems with a posteriori and heuristic stopping
item.description: arXiv:2610.38279v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A novel Data-driven STochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{D-STAR}) method is proposed for solving linear and nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems, which incorporates a data-driven drift and a stochastic diffusion mechanism. Both known and unknown noise level cases are accommodated by the method, thereby making the framework applicable to a broader range of practical inverse problems. For known noise level, a modified discrepancy principle is employed, whereas for unknown noise level, a heuristic stopping rule based solely on noisy data is developed. For each stopping rule, an appropriate diffusion term is defined and the well-posedness of the associated stochastic differential equation is demonstrated. The finite termination of \texttt{D-STAR} method under both stopping rules is established and its convergence to the exact solution in the noise-free setting is proved. For the noisy data, stability and the regularization property in the mean-square sense are further established. In addition, the uncertainty quantification of the proposed method and its comparison with the Stochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{SAR}) method under both rules are provided. Furthermore, it is shown that local minima arising in the Data-Driven Iteratively Regularized Landweber (\texttt{DDIRLI}) method may be escaped. Finally, detailed numerical experiments, including comparisons with existing \texttt{DDIRLI} and \texttt{SAR} methods, are presented on X-ray computed tomography and nonlinear schlieren tomography for both stopping rules, thereby demonstrating the performance of \texttt{D-STAR}.
item.dc:creator: Simran Soni, Harshit Bajpai, Ankik Kumar Giri

item.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.38386v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14{,}639{,}440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Elliott Mathewson

item.title: Capacity of the Hopfield-Hebbian dynamics with correlated patterns
item.description: arXiv:2610.38437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Allowing for small fraction of errors in retrieved stored binary patterns, Hopfield-Hebbian neural network (NN) associative memory dynamics [14] achieves linearly scaled capacity. The famous proportionality constant $\alpha_c\approx 0.14$ is obtained in a large dimensional scenario as the ratio of the number of reliably stored patterns $m$ and the patterns' length $n$ under the assumption that uniformly randomly chosen binary patterns are \emph{independent} among themselves. While such an idealized scenario is now well understood, more practical scenarios with correlated/noisy datasets remaining challenging even for classical statistical mechanics replica approaches. We consider precisely such practical settings where each \emph{archetype} pattern is replaced with $M$ correlated \emph{examples} with parameter $r$ governing the quality of correlation. We develop a powerful Random Duality Theory (RDT) based framework to analyze correlated data and already on the first level of RDT lifting obtain capacity characterizations that remarkably well match behavior exhibited through simulated dynamics. Moreover, characterizations explicitly feature correlation parameters $M$ and $r$, which allows to precisely determine their effects on phase-transitioning behavior of the underlying dynamics. Our results are also a well-fitting complement to the existing literature. Namely, to circumvent challenging statistical mechanics analyses, an alternative combination of spectral and replica methods is considered in [4]. We confirm that [4]'s elegant spectral characterizations are excellent approximations in the low correlated regime. At the same time, we also close the gap in the regimes with higher correlation levels where spectral methods deviate from the practical dynamics performance.
item.dc:creator: Mihailo Stojnic

item.title: Calibration of Passive Market Impact with a Queue-Sensitive Propagator Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.38442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a framework for calibrating passive market impact, defined as the price response to liquidity-providing limit orders, in contrast to the impact of liquidity-consuming market orders. We build on the model of Ouazzani Chahdi, Rosenbaum, and Szymanski (arxiv:2412.07461), which combines Hawkes-driven market-order flow with queue-reactive limit-order and cancellation dynamics. Within this model, we show that the price decomposes into a universal propagator term driven by signed order-flow imbalance and a state-dependent correction that captures the dependence of price sensitivity on volume at the best quotes. This decomposition links limit-order-book microstructure to standard propagator models and yields a regression on two observable signals: the propagator signal and the queue-weighted order-flow imbalance. We calibrate the model on high-frequency order-book data and find that the passive-impact term explains substantial variation in prices beyond the classical propagator, improving both model fit and the accuracy of predicted impact curves.
item.dc:creator: Yadh Hafsi, Fabrizio Lillo, Gr\'egoire Szymanski

item.title: Dimension-free exponential entropy quotients over $\mathbb{F}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^m$, and let $X'$ be an independent copy. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a subspace $G$ with $\dim G\le 2^{320(1+\varepsilon)/\varepsilon}H(X)$ such that $H(q_GX)\le(1+\varepsilon)(H(q_GX+q_GX')-H(q_GX))$. In particular, the quotient entropy is at most $(1+\varepsilon)(H(X+X')-H(X))$. The coefficient is independent of the ambient dimension, and its exponential order in $1/\varepsilon$ is necessary. The structural result is a logarithmic rigidity estimate for finite weighted families of laws with averaged subspace entropy sparsity. A common variational quotient controls both a family and its convolution family without decreasing the original family's normalized mean entropy defect. Posterior families preserve averaged sparsity, and a fresh-index argument combines a local-to-global estimate with the entropic Marton theorem to increase the defect ratio at a fixed multiplicative sparsity cost. We also obtain two-input almost-additivity and concentration of moderate-doubling sets on subspace cosets at the same exponential scale. The constants are not optimized.
item.dc:creator: Josiah Park

item.title: Curvature-Dimension Conditions Along Discrete Refinement Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.38538v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the sequence curvature--dimension condition $SCD(K,N)$ for complete refinement systems of finite metric probability spaces. The condition couples a transport action bound with entropy comparisons along a single probability section through the prescribed refinement layers. Within a bounded comparison range, we prove that midpoint comparisons on three consecutive layers characterize the condition on every fixed finite segment. If, in addition, the refinement sequence converges in the measured sense in its intrinsic bridge realization, then $SCD(K,N)$ is equivalent both to the vanishing of single-layer midpoint defects and to the entropic curvature--dimension condition $CD^{e}(K,N)$ of the limit. In the reverse direction, a $CD^{e}(K,N)$ bound on the limit yields quantitative recovery estimates that identify shrinking transport scales on which finite layers retain its second-order curvature comparison. These estimates are uniform over endpoint measures and include Dirac masses. Examples illustrate the effects of the refinement rule, the layer metrics and the reference measures.
item.dc:creator: Chen Tao

item.title: Graphon Colourings and Limits of Graph Partitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38599v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a framework for pure and mixed graphon colourings and use it to study the limiting behaviour of graph partition parameters under cut convergence. Pure colourings correspond to measurable partitions, while mixed colourings assign a probability distribution on the colour set to each point. We develop the representation, equivalence and convergence theory, and show that every mixed graphon colouring has an equivalent pure representative, possibly on a different probability space. For each fixed finite colour set, we establish compactness and describe the topology of coloured graph limits using the cut norm on graphons and the weak-$*$ topology on colourings. The usual coloured cut distance characterises convergence for pure colourings, but not for general mixed colourings. As applications, we prove that the Cheeger constant and modularity converge to their mixed graphon counterparts along cut-convergent graph sequences whose orders tend to infinity, assuming uniformly linear minimum degree and positive limiting edge density, respectively. Both mixed functionals are invariant under graphon equivalence. We also establish their continuity in cut distance on the corresponding classes of graphons, with a stability bound for the Cheeger constant. For modularity, we further characterise coloured graphons attaining extremal modularity values and prove attainment of the mixed optimum for each fixed number of colours. We also exhibit a graphon whose modularity supremum is not attained by any finite colouring.
item.dc:creator: Svante Janson, Tiffany Y. Y. Lo, Colin McDiarmid, Anda Skeja, Fiona Skerman

item.title: Well-Posedness and Regularity for a Modified Liquid Crystal Model with Transport Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.38641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove well-posedness for a stochastic Lin-Liu model of modified liquid crystals, coupling an incompressible fluid to a director field under transport and multiplicative noise. On smooth bounded domains in two dimensions, we prove global well-posedness for energy-class initial data, provided the leading coefficient of the polynomial director potential is positive. On the torus, we establish local well-posedness in time-weighted $L^p$-$L^q$ frameworks with Besov initial data, including regimes of low and negative regularity.
item.dc:creator: Gianmarco Del Sarto, Antoine Moneyron, Esm\'ee Theewis, Tarek Z\"{o}chling

item.title: Metropolized backward sampling for conditional sequential Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2610.38753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Particle Gibbs samplers with backward sampling are widely used for sampling the smoothing distribution of state-space models, but, with few particles, the new trajectory often coincides with the current one at many time steps. A known but rarely used remedy replaces the random selection of the final particle by a Metropolis--Hastings move which avoids the current particle. We show that, with backward sampling, this remedy only helps at the last time steps, because its effect on the update rates decays geometrically with the distance to the final time. We propose instead Metropolized backward sampling, which makes such a move at every step of the backward pass, forcibly switching trajectories whenever possible. Additionally, we introduce a coupled version which prevents proposing the current trajectory, maximizing the chances of an actual switch versus the current trajectory and performing perfect sampling when the state-space model has no observations, a feature not shared by backward sampling. We prove that, at every time step, both methods dominate backward sampling as they update the state more often and have smaller lag-one autocorrelations than it does. Our methods are drop-in replacements for backward sampling, and can be used to improve any particle Gibbs sampler.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Corenflos

item.title: Localization of generators of Markov processes via the Dynkin operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.38761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we consider a Feller process whose resolvent has the strong Feller property. Using the Dynkin operator of this process, we define local realizations of the generator on an open subset $U$ of its state space. In particular, this allows us to describe the generator of the process killed upon leaving a regular, open subset $U$ as a realization of a maximal operator subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. Besides the definition via the Dynkin operator, we also consider other possible definitions of such a local realization: a definition in terms of the unkilled semigroup, a definition based on approximation with elements of the generator and a probabilistic definition using martingales. Under mild additional assumptions, we prove that all these definitions are equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Markus Kunze, Jonathan Mui

item.title: A Hierarchical Online-Compression Approach to Proportional Subsets of Bounded Orthonormal Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.39025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(\phi_i)_{i=1}^n$ be an orthonormal system on a probability space with $\|\phi_i\|_\infty\leq L$. We prove that, for every $2\leq k<n$, there is a set $I$ of at least $n-k$ indices such that $$ \|f\|_2\leq CM_k\sqrt{\log(e+M_k)}\|f\|_1 $$ for every $f$ in the span of $(\phi_i)_{i\in I}$, where $M_k=L\sqrt{\frac{n}{k}\log(2k)}$. This replaces the logarithmic exponent $\frac{5}{2}$ in the corresponding theorem of Gu\'edon, Mendelson, Pajor, and Tomczak-Jaegermann by $\frac{1}{2}$. We also obtain a partition into two sets of cardinality $\frac{n}{2}+O(\sqrt n)$ for which both spans satisfy the resulting norm comparison, and for uniformly bounded systems the proportional estimate is $C\sqrt{\log n\log\log n}$ for sufficiently large $n$. This is the third paper in a series systematically using gradient descent as a proof mechanism in harmonic analysis, following the $\Lambda(p)$ and Bernoulli restricted isometry papers of Burstein, Iosevich, and Krause, and the descent here is entropic mirror descent. We represent each function in an $L_1$ ball by a probability measure of controlled relative entropy, and this entropy pays for the corrections to the predictions of its coefficients. Processing the thresholds from large to small, we obtain a single weighted bound for all the corrections, which we turn into a finite description of approximate coefficient squares and then into a conditional Rademacher estimate, and symmetrization completes the argument directly on the $L_1$ ball. We also record consequences for concentration and for recovery from coefficient measurements.
item.dc:creator: Will Burstein, Alex Iosevich, Ben Krause

item.title: Sharp potential and Brenier map $W_2$-stability for log-concave sources
item.description:
arXiv:2610.39272v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study stability of Brenier potentials and maps under changes of the target measure. Let $\kappa>0$, for a full support $\kappa$-strongly log-concave source $ho$, possibly with a non-smooth potential, the normalized transport potentials satisfy \[ \|u_\mu-u_
u\|_{L^2(ho)}\leqslant\sqrt{2/\kappa}\,W_2(\mu,
u) \] for arbitrary targets with finite second moments. The proof controls normalized Laguerre cell barycentres by their mass derivatives and centers the potential velocity to remove unbounded source cell locations. Bounded variation interpolation then yields the sharp map exponent $1/3$ for targets in a common compact set, \[ \left\Vert T_{\mu}-T_{
u}ight\Vert _{L^{2}(ho)}\leqslant \operatorname{Const} \cdot W_{2}\left( \mu,
uight) ^{1/3}. \] Sharpness of the exponents for both the potential and Brenier map stability are established.
item.dc:creator: Yuanlong Ruan

item.title: Limit Theorems and Optimal Policies for Flock Flight through Poisson Forests
item.description: arXiv:2610.39378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by birds flying through cluttered environments, Karaman and Frazzoli showed that high-speed flight through an ergodic random forest exhibits an ultimate speed limit: above a critical speed, almost surely no infinite collision-free trajectory exists for a single bird. This paper formulates a corresponding bulk-transport problem for many birds. We construct an explicit directed corridor network in a Poisson disk forest and impose a common temporal headway at its waypoints. The maximum current equals a minimum vertex-cut capacity and is achieved by repeated flight along vertex-disjoint paths. The same schedule maximizes completed traversals at every finite horizon, with constant forward speed and no internal waiting. For a forest belt of fixed depth, exact transverse superadditivity yields an almost-sure deterministic current-density limit. A uniform shape theorem for an asymmetric planar dual identifies the current when depth and width grow together. For diverging depth bounded by a constant times width, this current equals the width-first, depth-second limit and is independent of the positive aspect ratio. When diagonal corridors are available, bulk current is positive at sufficiently low obstacle intensity and zero at sufficiently high intensity. For stochastic demand, an upstream admission queue is stable at every rate below the finite-network capacity.
item.dc:creator: Lav R. Varshney

item.title: Fractal dimensions of paths on three-dimensional random-walk traces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39612v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study four paths that join the starting site to the final position of a simple random walk of \(N=L^2\) steps on the infinite cubic lattice. The paths are selected on the walk trace---the graph of visited sites and traversed bonds---by different rules: the undirected shortest path \(S_1\), the directed shortest path \(S_2\), the time-respecting shortest path \(S_3\), and the depth \(D_e\) of the final site in a depth-first-search tree. Monte Carlo simulations for \(L\) up to 32768 give mean lengths scaling as \(L^{d_O}\), with \(d_{S_1}=1.48005(9)\), \(d_{S_2}=1.49868(5)\), \(d_{S_3}=1.51205(5)\), and \(d_{D_e}=1.7099(7)\), so that \(d_{S_1}<d_{S_2}<d_{S_3}<d_{\rm LE}<d_{D_e}\), where $d_{\rm LE}=1.62400(5)$ is the known loop-erased-random-walk exponent. Imposing traversal directions increases the shortest-path exponent, and imposing time order increases it further; these constraints therefore change the scaling exponent, not only the amplitude. For every path, the standard deviation scales with the same exponent as the mean, so it is scale-invariant, unlike the visited-site mass; the rescaled length distributions collapse onto a finite-width scaling function. No analytical theory currently predicts these exponents; our results provide precise numerical benchmarks for future studies of path geometry on random-walk traces.
item.dc:creator: Qiyuan Shi, Xinyi Li, Youjin Deng

item.title: Emergence of the transformer architecture as the score of entropic laws of random measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.39614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the transformer architecture emerges as the score of last-token laws in a natural statistical model of language, where sentences are empirical measures of tokens, a language is a law on $P(S^d)$, and our prior belief is that sentences carry no structure at all. By the maximum-entropy principle, we select the law closest to this prior in relative entropy among those reproducing an observed sentence-level statistic. We discuss the relevance of the statistic in the posterior interaction between tokens and we build a statistic, able to capture that interaction, with Luce's choice axiom truncated at the lowest relational order. This procedure gives the softmax choice rule, with the attention cross-moment as its mean parameter. The query--key matrix is then the Lagrange multiplier of a maximum-entropy problem inside each sentence, and the value matrix the multiplier of the constraint over the language, so that the two are untied. Under the optimal entropic law we then show that a transformer head appears in the score of the last-token law. For ordered sentences, causal masking follows from the masked reference choice rule, and with a next-token cross-moment the score equals one causally masked attention head. We also discuss multi-head attention, weight-tied unembedding, and a heuristic reading of residual blocks as projected Langevin steps.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Greco

item.title: Random semigroups \'a la Gromov
item.description: arXiv:2610.39673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a model of random semigroups analogous to Gromov's density model for random groups. For a fixed number $n\ge 2$ of generators and a density parameter $\delta\in (0,1)$, we impose a uniformly chosen set of $\lfloor n^{2\delta l}\rfloor$ relations of the form $u=v$, where $u,v$ are distinct words of length at most $l$, and study the resulting semigroup as $l\to\infty$. We prove that, with overwhelming probability, above density $1/2$ the semigroup is trivial, while below density $1/2$ it contains a free subsemigroup of rank two, has a Golod-Shafarevich semigroup algebra over every field, and has a homomorphic image which generates a non-elementary hyperbolic group. We also show that the small cancellation condition $C(m)$ holds with overwhelming probability whenever $\delta<1/2m$. Finally, for $n\ge 3$, at critical density $1/2$ we obtain a subsequential limiting distribution on finite semigroups, with positive mass at the trivial semigroup and unbounded support in size. This contrasts with random groups, which have order at most two with overwhelming probability at critical density.
item.dc:creator: Guy Blachar, Be'eri Greenfeld, Margaret Shideler

item.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.39783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. Numerical experiments for a semiconductor inverse problem confirm that the proposed Bayesian all-at-once approach yields a speedup of approximately a factor of two, while having a comparable reconstruction quality as the conventional reduced-based setting.
item.dc:creator: Tram Thi Ngoc Nguyen, Fabian Schneider, Leila Taghizadeh

item.title: On record behaviours of returns for interval maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.39928v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $\mu$, a $\mu$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.
item.dc:creator: Boyuan Zhao

item.title: Level Crossing Rate Bounds for Products of Independent Nonstationary Fading Processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.39950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a unified framework for the instantaneous total level crossing rate (LCR) of products of independent positive nonstationary fading processes. Universal upper and lower bounds are first derived from an exact decomposition of the product derivative and signed crossing imbalance, requiring only factor-wise crossing statistics. We then introduce the drifting Gaussian-derivative (DGD) class, in which each conditional derivative is Gaussian with possibly nonzero drift. For products of DGD factors, an exact Gaussian-mixture representation yields bounds that jointly capture aggregate drift and derivative fluctuations. The lower bound reduces under stationarity to a known $\ell_2$ bound, whereas, to the best of the author's knowledge, the upper bound is new even in the stationary case. Furthermore, the bounds are asymptotically exact in drift-dominated regimes. The framework is specialized to nonstationary Double-Rayleigh fading and to quasi-identically distributed DGD factors, with closed forms for products of $\alpha$-$\mu$ envelopes. Numerical results show that the DGD bounds closely bracket the exact LCR.
item.dc:creator: Pl\'inio Santini Dester

item.title: Optimal subtrees of finite metric graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a metric graph analog of a classical extremal problem for Riemann surfaces studied by Teichm\"uller, Jenkins, Strebel, and others. In particular, we prove that on any finite metric graph with a marked point, there is a unique open subtree which maximizes a metric graph analog of the reduced modulus, and we also give an equivalent characterization of this optimal subtree in terms of balanced harmonic measures.
item.dc:creator: Levi Haunschmid-Sibitz, Fredrik Viklund, David Witt Nystr\"om

item.title: Ricci curvature of semigroup walks on graphs and generator representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an operator-theoretic framework for the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of (one-parameter families of) random walks generated by positive semigroups on graphs. On a metrically complete graph $(G,d)$ that is $d$-locally finite, we introduce a class of admissible semigroup random walks whose infinitesimal first-order approximation is itself a random walk. We prove that the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of an admissible semigroup random walk is well-defined and completely determined by its first-order approximation. We then establish a variational representation of the curvature of random walks in terms of a notion of the initial-time generator. This representation applies in particular to admissible semigroup random walks. Finally, we use this representation to define an operator-theoretic Ollivier--Ricci curvature for operators acting on spaces of functions over general metric spaces and establish sufficient conditions for well-definedness. This framework contains, in particular, Markovian random walks associated with discrete Laplacians.
item.dc:creator: Sajjad Lakzian

item.title: Symmetries and exact solutions of stochastic differential equations: the CIR model
item.description: arXiv:2610.40316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is well known that in the celebrated Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process for interest rates there exists a critical relation among the model parameters. In the present work, we explain this critical relation by studying the symmetries of the stochastic differential equation and compute the solution of the model using this symmetry. In this way we also recover results of a recent paper where this property has been studied within a broader context by analyzing the relationships among the symmetries of stochastic differential equations and their corresponding forward Kolmogorov equations.
item.dc:creator: Miguel A. Rodr\'iguez

item.title: Terminal Localization of Empirical Reverse Diffusions under Singular Score Errors
item.description: arXiv:2610.40374v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a finite empirical target, the exact reverse diffusion is driven toward training points by an attraction whose strength diverges as the forward noising time decreases to zero. We study whether this terminal localization persists under progressively measurable score errors that may themselves be singular. For reverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusions, from an arbitrary initial law and under a deterministic error envelope \(E\) imposed along the perturbed trajectory satisfying \(t\int_t^T E(\sigma)/\sigma\,d\sigma\to0\), we prove almost-sure convergence to a training point, together with explicit uniform bounds on a terminal window with probability arbitrarily close to one. Every training point has positive terminal probability, although the terminal selection probabilities need not match the empirical weights. The results cover power-law errors \(E(t)=O(t^{-\gamma})\), \(0<\gamma<1\), including infinite squared-error energy. For suitable errors in this range, the exact and perturbed full path laws can be mutually singular while their terminal laws share the same finite support. For suitable switched perturbations at the critical scale \(t^{-1}\), arbitrarily small positive amplitudes can produce a nonzero terminal displacement with arbitrarily high probability. These results quantify stochastic robustness of empirical terminal attraction without requiring absolute continuity of the full path laws.
item.dc:creator: Zhonghua Liao

item.title: Zero-freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.40510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study antiferromagnetic spin systems on random regular graphs through the lens of the phase transitions characterized by the complex zeros of the partition function. Our motivating examples include the hardcore model and the antiferromagnetic Potts model (including proper $q$-colorings at $\beta=0$). For both models on random $d$-regular graphs, we establish, with high probability over the graph, zero-free regions throughout the interior of the replica-symmetric regime. Asymptotically, this regime extends up to tree occupation density $$\alpha < \alpha_{\mathrm{RSB}}(d) = (2\log d - 2\log\log d + 2 - 2\log 2 + o_d(1))/d$$ for the hardcore model and up to degree $$d < d_{\mathrm{RSB}}(q) = (2q-1)\log q - 2\log 2 + o_q(1)$$ for proper $q$-colorings. Leveraging the standard algorithmic implications of zero-freeness, we obtain deterministic polynomial-time algorithms that multiplicatively approximate the corresponding partition functions at fixed rational parameters throughout this regime, with high probability over the graph. Our algorithmic guarantees significantly improve upon prior work and extend beyond the parameter ranges reached by previously known search algorithms. To establish our results, we first develop reinforced small subgraph conditioning, which resolves short-cycle fluctuations in the complex plane by lifting classical small subgraph conditioning on random regular graphs to random holomorphic functions. Second, we overcome the standard second-moment barrier caused by the exponential blowup of the bare second moment inside the replica-symmetric phase, by showing that replica symmetry implies a nonpositive Bethe functional and upgrading planted overlap concentration to an exponentially small bound, which enables a typical-graph truncation that controls complex second moments up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold.
item.dc:creator: Zejia Chen, Chunyang Wang, Xinyuan Zhang

item.title: Power Adjusting Games Under Block-Dependent Pool Payout Schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.40558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Advanced power adjusting block withholding attacks such as PAW and T-PAW have been analyzed so far under a global-reset version of the proportional scheme (GRP), which is rarely used in practice. In this paper, we analyze T-PAW, which contains FAW and PAW as special cases, under the block-dependent payout schemes deployed in practice: Pay-Per-Last-N-Shares (PPLNS), round-based Proportional (PROP) and exponential-decay (EXP). We derive the revenue ratios analytically, by renewal arguments for PPLNS and through the stationary carry process of an open round for PROP and EXP. We further introduce Power Adjusting Hopping (PAH), where an adversary of any size adjusts its power allocation towards the pool according to the blockwork age of the round without withholding any block, and derive its revenue ratios under PROP and EXP. We show that GRP misestimates the T-PAW gain in a scheme-dependent direction: it overstates the gain under PROP up to an order of magnitude and understates it under EXP for the original slush decay rate. PROP is highly vulnerable to PAH, while EXP faces a trade-off: a slow decay invites PAH and a fast decay invites T-PAW. PPLNS is the least vulnerable scheme: it is immune to PAH and it mitigates, but does not eliminate, T-PAW. All analytical results are verified by Monte Carlo simulations.
item.dc:creator: Mustafa Doger, Sennur Ulukus

item.title: Nearly-Optimal Time-Sample Trade-off in Consensus Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.40562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How does the number of sampled opinions affect the time required to reach consensus in distributed consensus dynamics? We study the synchronous $h$-\textsf{Majority}, in which every node independently samples $h$ nodes uniformly at random with replacement in each round and adopts a most frequent sampled opinion, breaking ties uniformly at random. We show that $h$-\textsf{Majority} achieves the nearly-optimal trade-off between the sample size and the consensus time, among a broad class of consensus dynamics. In particular, we prove the following results. For every sample size $h \ge 3$ and for every initial configuration, we prove that the process reaches consensus with high probability within $\widetilde{O}\left(1+\min\left\{\frac{1}{\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\}},\frac{\sqrt{n}}{h}\right\}\right)$ rounds, where $n$ is the number of nodes and $p_{\max}$ is the largest initial fraction of nodes supporting any single opinion. This is the first bound on the consensus time for $h$-\textsf{Majority} that holds for every $h\ge3$ and every initial configuration. When the initially most popular opinion has a sufficiently large lead over every other opinion, we show that all nodes adopt this opinion with high probability within $O(\log n/\min\{h^2p_{\max},1\})$ rounds. We establish a matching lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors for any fixed update rule that treats all opinions symmetrically and that selects either a sampled opinion or the node's current opinion.
item.dc:creator: Francesco d'Amore, Joel Rybicki, Nobutaka Shimizu, Takeharu Shiraga, Robin Vacus

item.title: On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up to Kesten-Stigum
item.description: arXiv:2610.40598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give the first polynomial-time algorithm to estimate the partition function of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on the uniformly random $d$-regular graph to arbitrarily high accuracy for all inverse temperatures up to the Kesten-Stigum threshold. This is the entire regime in which the model is "replica symmetric," and is conjectured to be optimal for polynomial-time counting and sampling. To achieve our algorithmic result, we establish the absence of Fisher zeros for the partition function in a constant-width strip around the interval from $0$ up to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, with high probability over the randomness of the input graph. AI Disclosure: The overarching vision and proof architecture were developed solely by the authors without AI input. GPT 5.5 Pro was used, with extensive guidance from the authors, for only a few minor technical aspects of the proof. The authors independently verified correctness and wrote everything by hand. We take full responsibility for its contents. A more detailed statement can be found in Section 1.2.
item.dc:creator: Ferenc Bencs, Brice Huang, Daniel Z. Lee, Kuikui Liu, Guus Regts

item.title: Diffusion Processes on $p$-Wasserstein Space over Banach Space
item.description: arXiv:2402.15130v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To study diffusion processes on the p-Wasserstein space $\mathscr P_p$ for $p\in [1,\infty)$ over a separable, reflexive Banach space $X$, we present a criterion on the quasi-regularity of Dirichlet forms in $L^2(\mathscr P_p,\Lambda)$ for a reference probability $\Lambda$ on $\mathscr P_p$. It is formulated in terms of an upper bound condition with the uniform norm of the intrinsic derivative. We find a versatile class of quasi-regular local Dirichlet forms on $\mathscr P_p$ by using images of Dirichlet forms on the tangent space $L^p(X\to X,\mu_0)$ at a reference point $\mu_0\in\mathscr P_p$. The Ornstein--Uhlenbeck type Dirichlet form and process on $\mathscr P_2$ are an important example in this class. We derive an $L^2$-estimate for the corresponding heat kernel and an integration by parts formula for the invariant measure.
item.dc:creator: Panpan Ren, Feng-Yu Wang, Simon Wittmann

item.title: Convergence of stochastic integrals with applications to transport equations and conservation laws with noise
item.description: arXiv:2404.16157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Convergence of stochastic integrals driven by Wiener processes $W_n$, with $W_n \to W$ almost surely in $C_t$, is crucial in analyzing SPDEs. Our focus is on the convergence of the form $\int_0^T V_n\, \mathrm{d} W_n \to \int_0^T V\, \mathrm{d} W$, where $\{V_n\}$ is bounded in $L^p(\Omega \times [0,T];X)$ for a Banach space $X$ and some finite $p > 2$. This is challenging when $V_n$ converges to $V$ weakly in the temporal variable. We supply convergence results to handle stochastic integral limits when strong temporal convergence is lacking. A key tool is a uniform mean $L^1$ time translation estimate on $V_n$, an estimate that is easily verified in many SPDEs. However, this estimate alone does not guarantee strong compactness of $(\omega,t)\mapsto V_n(\omega,t)$. Our findings, especially pertinent to equations exhibiting singular behavior, are substantiated by establishing several stability results for stochastic transport equations and conservation laws.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth H. Karlsen, Peter H. C. Pang

item.title: Coarse embeddability, $L^1$-compression and Percolations on General Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2406.04222v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a locally finite, connected graph has a coarse embedding into a Hilbert space if and only if there exist bond percolations with arbitrarily large marginals and two-point function vanishing at infinity. We further show that the decay of the two-point function is stretched exponential with stretching exponent $\alpha\in[0,1]$ if and only if the $L^1$-compression exponent of the graph is at least $\alpha$, leading to a probabilistic characterization of this exponent. These results are new even in the particular setting of Cayley graphs of finitely generated groups. The proofs build on new probabilistic methods introduced recently by the authors to study group-invariant percolation on Cayley graphs [28,29], which are now extended to the general, non-symmetric situation of graphs to study their coarse embeddability and $L^1$-compression exponents.
item.dc:creator: Chiranjib Mukherjee, Konstantin Recke

item.title: Flexible random graph modelling for cell-cell interactions
item.description: arXiv:2502.21083v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we explore generalisations to a random digraph model designed for modelling cell-cell interactions (RaCInG). In its baseline model -- tested both theoretically and in biological practice -- a fixed number of arcs are assigned uniformly at random to vertices that have suitable types to accept them. Generalisations to this model are explored in two directions: constructing an undirected graph version of the model, and incorporating spatial information. Both directions are driven by biological demands: better interpretability and adaptation to technological advances. We show not only that these generalisations are theoretically possible within the framework of RaCInG, but that they can be made rigorous, proving that RaCInG creates a flexible random graph framework to model cell-cell interactions.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Complex Networks, Volume 14, Issue 6, December 2026, cnag039
item.dc:creator: Mike van Santvoort, Pim van der Hoorn

item.title: Brownian motion and stochastic areas on complex partial flag manifolds with blocks of equal size
item.description: arXiv:2511.06047v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a Brownian motion on complex partial flag manifolds with blocks of equal size as a matrix-valued diffusion from a Brownian motion on the unitary group. This construction leads to an explicit expression for the characteristic function of the joint distribution of the stochastic areas on these manifolds. The limit law of these stochastic areas is shown to be a multivariate Cauchy distribution with independent and identically distributed entries. By relating the area functionals on flag manifolds to the winding functional on the complex Stiefel manifold, we establish new results about simultaneous Brownian windings on the complex Stiefel manifold. To establish these results, this work introduces a new family of diffusions, which generalise both the Jacobi processes on the simplex and the Hermitian Jacobi processes.
item.dc:creator: Teije Kuijper

item.title: A Class of Gaussian Fields on $\mathbb{Z}_q^d$
item.description: arXiv:2602.19469v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Complex Gaussian fields $(g_x)$ on $\mathbb{Z}_q^d$ are constructed from a class of reversible long range random walks $(X_t)_{t\in \mathbb{N}}$ on $\mathbb{Z}_q^d$ in \citeauthor{GM2025a} (\citeyear{GM2025a}). The construction is from taking $\mathbb{E}\big [g_x\bar{g}_y\big ]= (1-\alpha)G(x,y;\alpha)$, where $G(x,y;\alpha)$ is the Green function of a random walk with killing in each transition at rate $1-\alpha$. Another real Gaussian field $(h^\circ_x=\Re g_x + \Im g_x)$ is constructed such that also Cov$(h^\circ_x,h^\circ_y) = (1-\alpha)G(x,y;\alpha)$. If the random walk is not reversible, then a different approach is needed because $G(x,y;\alpha)$ is not exchangeable in $x,y$. It is shown that there exists two real Gaussian fields $(h^+_x)$, $(h^-_y)$ such that Cov$(h^+_x,h^-_y) = (1-\alpha)G(x,y;\alpha)$. A decomposition of the Gaussian field $(g_x)$ into a sum of independent Gaussian random variables is made. By letting $q\to \infty$ the Gaussian field becomes defined from an infinite-dimensional random walk on a torus. The random walk model is also extended to $d=\infty$ by considering a de Finetti random walk where entries in the increments of the random walk are exchangeable. A limit Gaussian field on $\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from a central limit theorem approach. The transform of this Gaussian field, which is again a Gaussian field, is calculated. It has a simpler covariance matrix than the original field. The Hamiltonian connected to the Gaussian field is calculated. A limit theorem for the partition function arising from the Hamiltonian is found.
item.dc:creator: Robert Griffiths, Shuhei Mano

item.title: Fractal dimension of singular times for SPDEs: Energy bounds, criticality, and weak-strong uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2602.21981v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For several physically relevant SPDEs, it is known that global weak solutions coexist with local strong ones. Typically, weak-strong uniqueness results are known, and ensure that the global and strong solutions coincide as long as the latter exist. Times at which a weak solution does not coincide with a strong one are called singular times. Determining their fractal dimension is fundamental to capturing the regularity of weak solutions. We introduce a probabilistic notion of singular times for a wide class of semilinear SPDEs. We show that sets of singular times have fractal dimension (i.e., Hausdorff and/or Minkowski) at most $ 1-\ell\, \mathsf{Exc}$, where $\ell$ and $\mathsf{Exc}$ are the time integrability and the excess of spatial regularity compared to the critical regularity of the energy bound associated with weak solutions, respectively. Moreover, their corresponding $(1-\ell\,\mathsf{Exc} )$-dimensional measure is zero. We formulate and apply our theory to annealed strong Leray-Hopf solutions of 3D Navier-Stokes equations (NSEs) with physically relevant noises, including rough Kraichnan and Lie transport. In particular, we extend the fundamental $1/2$-dimensional bound of Leray and Scheffer on singular times for 3D NSEs to the stochastic setting, and we prove new conditional results under supercritical Serrin's conditions, irrespective of the roughness of the noise. Our framework is new even in the deterministic case, and provides the first partial regularity results for weak solutions to SPDEs with multiplicative noise.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Agresti

item.title: Exit times from time-dependent random domains: continuity, weak convergence, and exit-time profiles
item.description: arXiv:2604.03129v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study exit times from time-dependent domains under joint perturbations of the trajectory and the domain. Representing a moving domain as the negativity set of a continuous barrier on space-time, we reduce the exit problem to a one-dimensional first-passage problem for the scalarized path, namely the barrier evaluated along the trajectory. Our first main result is a deterministic continuity theorem: the exit-time functional is continuous, under Skorokhod J1 convergence of the path and locally uniform convergence of the barrier, at every configuration satisfying an explicit nontangency condition (NT). This condition is sharp: it characterizes the continuity set of the functional. As a consequence, exit times converge in distribution whenever paths and barriers converge jointly in distribution and the limiting pair satisfies (NT) almost surely; no independence or other structural restriction between trajectory and domain is required. Our second main result is a functional limit theorem: the profile of exit times indexed by the barrier level, regularized to be right-continuous on a compact level interval, converges in distribution in the Skorokhod M1 topology under the same joint convergence, provided the limiting pair satisfies (NT) almost surely at the two end levels; an example shows that J1 convergence can fail. Verification routes for (NT) are provided, including a non-characteristic criterion for Ito diffusions. The framework is illustrated by two Donsker-type examples; in the second one, the domain is random, is approximated jointly with the trajectory, and is coupled to the state.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Guillaume (CY Cergy Paris University)

item.title: Persistence of the Wiener sausage: sampling stability and limit theorems for Betti-curve functionals of planar Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2604.03130v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the persistent homology of the offset filtration generated by the range of a planar Brownian motion with constant nonzero drift (Wiener sausages of increasing radius). We prove what are, to our knowledge, the first law of large numbers and central limit theorem for its smoothed Betti-curve functionals. For every bounded Borel weight $\psi$ supported in a compact radius window $[r_0,r_1]\subset(0,\infty)$, the functional $\Phi_\psi(T)=\int_{r_0}^{r_1}\beta_1(T,r)\psi(r)\,dr$, where $\beta_1(T,r)$ counts the holes of the radius-$r$ sausage at time $T$, satisfies $\Phi_\psi(T)/T\to\rho_\psi$ almost surely and in every $L^p$, for a deterministic constant $\rho_\psi$. This yields a finite positive Betti-curve intensity measure on the radius axis, which we identify as absolutely continuous through a fixed-radius law of large numbers along regeneration times, valid at almost every radius. We also prove Gaussian fluctuations at scale $\sqrt{T}$, for one weight and jointly for finitely many, with a Green-Kubo variance over the regeneration cycles. The proof combines a renewal structure along the drift direction, obtained by the method of Sznitman and Zerner without invoking the strong Markov property at the cut times, with a Mayer-Vietoris control of the non-additivity of topology under concatenation and a deterministic bound on the integrated hole count of a planar offset proved in a companion paper. A sampling theorem bounds the bottleneck distance between the diagram of the continuous filtration and that of a time-sampled point cloud by the pathwise modulus of continuity, placing these objects in a data-analytic framework.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Guillaume

item.title: Moderate deviations for the Maki--Thompson rumour model
item.description: arXiv:2605.08629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the classical Maki--Thompson rumour model with $n$ initially ignorant individuals and one initial spreader. The final number of ignorants, divided by $n$, is known to satisfy the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and the large deviation principle. We establish a moderate deviation principle for fluctuations of this proportion of order $b_n/\sqrt n$, where $b_n\to\infty$ and $b_n^2=o(\log n)$. The proof rests on the exact final-size distribution, sharp asymptotics for the associated automata numbers, and a uniform point probability expansion at the moderate deviation scale. Numerical comparisons of both tails illustrate the intermediate scale and the effect of early extinction on upper tail probabilities.
item.dc:creator: Shaochen Wang, Guangyu Yang

item.title: Continuous stochastic flows driven by white noise and their duals
item.description: arXiv:2606.12143v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a class of continuous stochastic flows driven by a space-time white noise and characterize their dual flows by explicit stochastic differential equations. A key ingredient of the proof is the convergence of solutions under coefficient approximations. As an application, we derive the dual flows in two illustrative examples, the squared Bessel flow and the Jacobi flow. We also introduce a new model of polynomially self-repelling (PSR) flow and show that it enjoys a self-duality property.
item.dc:creator: Yaolin Yu

item.title: The Ornstein$-$Uhlenbeck process on $\mathscr P_2$ with a volatility operator
item.description: arXiv:2606.14917v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze diffusion processes ${(\mu_t)}_{t\geq 0}$ on the $2$-Wasserstein space $\mathscr P_2$ over $\mathbb R^d$, which can be classified as Ornstein--Uhlenbeck processes by means of their Fukushima decomposition. Characteristically for this class, $ | \mu_t|_2^2-|\mu_0|_2^2-2ct+2\int_0 ^t|\mu_s|_2^2\,d s,\, t\geq 0,$ is a martingale, where $c\in(0,\infty)$ is a constant and $|\mu_t|_2:=(\int_{\mathbb R^d}x^{\text{T}} x\mu_t(d x ))^{1/2}$ denotes the second moment. Making a particular choice from this class, we obtain a process ${(\mu_t)}_{t\geq 0}$ such that all moments exist and ${\mu_t(\theta)}-{\mu_0(\theta)}-\int_0 ^t\mu_s\big(\Delta \theta-\langle \text{id}_{\mathbb R^d},\nabla \theta\rangle\big)d s$, $t\geq 0$, is a martingale for each multivariate polynomial $\theta:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$.
item.dc:creator: Martin Grothaus, Simon Wittmann

item.title: Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.00800v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Minkowski normed space is the Euclidean space equipped with a (possibly asymmetric) uniformly convex and smooth norm, forming a particular class of Finsler manifolds. We construct a stochastic process with one-dimensional time marginal densities given by the fundamental solution to the nonlinear Finsler heat equation in Minkowski normed spaces. This process is constructed as a solution to a singular McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and constitutes a nonlinear Markov process in the sense of McKean. We show that solutions to this stochastic differential equation are pathwise unique, and, thus, probabilistically strong solutions, though the equation has singular coefficients beyond the subcritical regime. Since our construction is a natural extension of the construction of standard Brownian motion from the standard heat kernel, we call this process \emph{Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces.} Furthermore, we obtain a universality property, namely that whichever Minkowski norm is chosen, the radial part of this process is the standard Bessel process. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first construction of stochastic processes associated with nonlinear heat equation in Finslerian spaces.
item.dc:creator: Shin-ichi Ohta, Marco Rehmeier, Kohei Suzuki

item.title: A Sharp Joint Bias-Energy Envelope for Radial Clipping
item.description: arXiv:2608.18999v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Radial clipping does two things at once: it cuts off the part of a vector outside a ball and leaves a bounded vector inside the ball. The part cut off defines the residual. For a random vector, we study the magnitude of the bias in the mean and the energy, defined as the centered second moment of the clipped vector. Controlling these effects is important in stochastic optimization with heavy tails, where the choice of the clipping threshold affects convergence bounds for algorithms. In the deterministic problem, for a fixed threshold $\tau>0$, $1\le p\le2$, and nonnegative coefficients $\alpha,\beta$, we find the smallest constant that simultaneously bounds the residual and energy in terms of $\lVert x\rVert^p$. This same constant remains sharp in the stochastic counterpart for random vectors in a Hilbert space. We also find the exact supremum of the corresponding linear combination of normalized bias and energy for arbitrary $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$. We then give a geometric picture in the energy-bias plane. Varying the weights, we describe the smallest closed convex region containing all normalized pairs and the attainable set itself, identifying unattainable boundary values. Every attainable pair at a fixed threshold can be realized by a real-valued random variable taking at most two values. We also consider all thresholds simultaneously. For any integrable random vector in a Hilbert space, we construct a single $\mathbb R^3$-valued random vector preserving its norm distribution, bias magnitude, and energy simultaneously at every threshold $\tau>0$. Finally, we apply the joint bound to risk-adjusted reinsurance costs for a prescribed retention threshold and to the logarithmic shortfall of a clipped portfolio strategy relative to any constant-fraction strategy. AI was used in preparing this paper (see Section 8).
item.dc:creator: Danila Litvinov

item.title: An approximate zero bias transformation for random sums: Applications to sampling with outliers, auto insurance, and generative AI
item.description: arXiv:2608.27143v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop $L^1$ bounds for the difference between a test function of a random sum and a standard normal random variable, where the summands are assumed to be independent but not necessarily identically distributed. The bounds are obtained through a new version of the approximate zero bias transformation specifically developed for random sums. Although the identical distribution assumption is relaxed, the bounds are of order $1/\sqrt{n}$, matching the order of existing bounds in the literature under the same distributional assumption on the number of summands. The main results are then applied to three real-world settings: random sums obtained from simple random sampling with outliers, total insurance claims, and generative AI response times.
item.dc:creator: Wasamon Jantai, Nathakhun Wiroonsri

item.title: Limit shape, avalanches, and stabilisation of abelian sandpiles on comb lattices
item.description: arXiv:2609.21359v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study two aspects of the abelian sandpile model on comb lattices. First, we prove that the infinite-volume limit of the stationary measures is supported on the saturated configuration. We then investigate the shape of avalanches induced by adding a particle at the origin in finite boxes of size $(2n+1)\times(2n+1)$ around the origin. In the stationary distribution on these finite boxes, we show that avalanches reach the boundary along the vertical teeth with probability tending to $1$, while the horizontal spread is of order $\sqrt{n}$. Finally, we establish that the single-source limit shape for abelian sandpiles on the comb lattice agrees with the corresponding limit shapes for the divisible sandpile, internal diffusion-limited aggregation (IDLA), and rotor-router aggregation models. This establishes limit shape universality on the comb lattice.
item.dc:creator: Robin Kaiser, Ecaterina Sava-Huss, Julia \"Uberbacher

item.title: A Functional Central Limit Theorem for Locally Stationary Time Series in Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.25791v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a functional central limit theorem for locally stationary time series in a separable Banach space $B$. The result requires no type-2 or cotype assumptions and thus covers spaces central to functional data analysis, such as $C([0,1])$ and $L^p([0,1])$. Under moment conditions, summable physical dependence coefficients and a bracketing entropy condition controlling the infinite-dimensional tails, the centered partial sum process converges weakly in $D([0,1],B)$ to a centered Gaussian process, whose covariance is the integrated local long-run covariance, an element of the projective tensor product. We also obtain a stochastic integral representation with respect to a cylindrical Brownian motion. As the limit depends on the unknown long-run covariance, we prove consistency of a block multiplier bootstrap for the partial sum process. This yields CUSUM tests for a constant mean of the full process, based on arbitrary continuous seminorms and valid under a time-varying long-run covariance. For linear projections, we derive a self-normalized test with a pivotal limit. In simulations, the supremum norm test detects localized changes that its $L^2$ counterpart largely misses, and applications to EEG and temperature data illustrate the methodology. Examples in $C([0,1])$ and $W^{1,p}_0([0,1])$ show how the entropy condition can be verified.
item.dc:creator: Florian Heinrichs, Luis-Alberto Rodr\'iguez

item.title: Classification of commutation relation for multi-chordal SLE
item.description: arXiv:2610.04362v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the linear solution spaces of the chordal Belavin--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (BPZ) equations, which arise in Dub\'edat's commutation relations for multiple Schramm--Loewner evolutions (SLE). Without imposing growth conditions, we determine the subspaces selected by successive conformal Ward identities and their exact dimensions. For every $\kappa>0$ and BPZ spectral parameter $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$, we determine the spectrum and Jordan structure of the translation operator. When $\lambda=0$ and $\kappa\in(0,8)$, we further determine all admissible scaling exponents and the dimensions of the corresponding translation-invariant solution spaces. A triangular change of derivative coordinates yields a first-order system of rational Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov type, allowing us to represent the Ward operators explicitly and reduce the classification to finite-dimensional linear algebra. For $2N$ boundary points and $\kappa\in(0,8)$, translation-invariant BPZ solutions with $\lambda=0$ and the homogeneity required by M\"obius covariance automatically satisfy the third Ward identity and the usual power-law bound. This recovers, under weaker assumptions, the Catalan dimension formula previously established by Flores and Kleban. At $\kappa=8$, the third Ward identity imposes an additional constraint when $N\ge2$, but the full M\"obius-covariant solution space still has Catalan dimension, establishing completeness of the partition functions constructed from uniform spanning trees. Finally, at $\kappa=4$ and $\lambda>0$, we construct an explicit basis of positive BPZ solutions and identify its elements as partition functions for level lines of a Gaussian free field with suitable harmonic means.
item.dc:creator: Mo Chen, Chongzhi Huang, Hao Wu

item.title: A shape theorem for a radially excited random walk in dimensions $d \ge 2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.12138v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: NOTE (October 2026): This paper has been superseded by the joint paper "Limit shapes for centrally excited walks", by Ahmed Bou-Rabee, Tuan-Minh Nguyen, Yuval Peres and Arvind Singh (arXiv:2610.10162), which brings together the results and ideas of three independent drafts. We consider a once-excited random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \ge 2$, where the walk on its first visit has a bias of constant strength $\beta>0$ toward the origin and moves like a simple symmetric random walk on subsequent visits to that site. We show that the walk is recurrent and prove an almost sure spherical shape theorem: the trace after $n$ steps is asymptotically a Euclidean ball centered at the origin, with radius proportional to $n^{1/(d+1)}$, and the local times have an asymptotically conical profile. This result confirms a conjecture of Kozma (2007) on the shape of the trace for this model.
item.dc:creator: Arvind Singh

item.title: Sums of two dependent uniform random variables: a characterization by joint tail bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24197v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Which laws can the sum of two uniform random variables have when nothing is known about how they depend on each other? For three or more uniform summands, convex order gives the answer; for two it does not, and the question has been open. We show that the attainable laws are exactly those that satisfy a family of explicit joint bounds on sums of tail probabilities, one bound for each finite set of thresholds. For laws with a density at most one, convex order alone decides. For densities at most two, convex order implies the simplest of the joint bounds, and the constant two cannot be raised for single-threshold bounds. The number of thresholds a law needs is set by the spacing of its atoms, not by how many atoms it has.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal

item.title: Bulk universality of scaling limits for the almost Hermitian Coulomb gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.25364v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Inspired by the recent approach to edge universality of Cronvall and Wennman, we prove several local universality results for scaling limits in the bulk in the almost Hermitian regime, as well as associated results relating to reproducing kernel spaces of the Fock type.
item.dc:creator: Yacin Ameur

item.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
item.description: arXiv:2610.29206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established.
item.dc:creator: Dmitriy F. Kuznetsov

item.title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
item.description: arXiv:2610.30382v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $\theta_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge \theta_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $\theta_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^\beta$, for any given $\beta\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $\theta_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.
item.dc:creator: Jacopo Borga, Victor Dubach

item.title: Stationary Coexistence in Stochastic Gause Systems with General Trophic Responses
item.description: arXiv:2610.37372v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study stationary coexistence in stochastic Gause predator-prey systems with independent multiplicative environmental noise and trophic responses depending on both population densities. A weighted population balance cancels the trophic interaction and yields moments of order greater than one without imposing predator self-regulation. These estimates give a direct occupation-measure proof of a sufficient coexistence criterion based on prey establishment and predator invasion of the prey-only stationary environment. For responses whose rare-predator limit is strictly increasing and whose value at positive predator density never exceeds that limit, we also establish necessity of positive predator invasion whenever the prey-only stationary law exists. If the prey per-capita growth attains its global maximum at zero, interior stationarity itself forces prey establishment, giving a necessary-and-sufficient criterion beyond logistic growth. Logistic and bounded saturating growth laws provide explicit Gamma and beta-prime resident distributions. Applications include Holling, Ivlev, Beddington-DeAngelis, and Crowley-Martin responses. Responses with the same rare-predator limit share the coexistence threshold, although predator interference changes the interior distribution. Reproducible quadrature and simulations illustrate this distinction. The analysis builds on existing stochastic persistence theory and identifies precisely the additional comparison argument needed for necessity, including exclusion of interior invariant measures at zero predator invasion.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'es S\'anchez, Leon A. Valencia, Jorge M. Ramirez Osorio

item.title: The Price of Failure Risk: Clipped Barrier Policy Gradients with Convex Regularization
item.description: arXiv:2411.19193v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In many control problems, actions consume a resource budget, such as a wear allowance, and the probability of exhausting it within a given horizon must stay below a tolerance. A simple, widely used approach is to augment the state with the remaining budget, subtract an interior barrier from the utility and penalize exhaustion, so that policy-gradient methods can be applied unchanged. We clip the combined one-step reward from below at a level m to keep the returns of exploratory policies finite. The clip level is a price of failure risk, since the clipped value decomposes exactly into the utility before failure, the cost of the interior margin and m times a geometric failure risk. Consequently, an approximately optimal policy maximizes utility net of margin cost among policies with no greater risk. Its risk exceeds that of any comparison policy by at most order 1/m and can be certified from its value or from validation data. Our main result proves exponential convergence of the population policy-gradient flow for every parameter regularizer that is convex along generalized geodesics and sufficiently strong relative to the price. This extends the mean-field analysis from relative entropy to weight decay and to finite networks. Relative entropy adds parameter noise and a pull toward a prior, whereas weight decay provides only the pull. Action regularization bounds changes in failure risk by the relative entropy to a reference policy. The bounds are evaluated on an exact maintenance benchmark, a fuel-tank controller, a solvable flow and a benchmark-suite task.
item.dc:creator: Pekka Malo, Lauri Viitasaari, Antti Suominen, Eeva Vilkkumaa, Olli Tahvonen

item.title: A particle system approach towards the global well-posedness of master equations for potential mean field games of control
item.description: arXiv:2412.11742v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies the $N$-particle systems as well as the HJB/master equations for a class of generalized mean field control (MFC) problems and the corresponding potential mean field games of control (MFGC). A local in time classical solution for the HJB equation is generated via a probabilistic approach based on the mean field maximum principle. Given an extension of the so called displacement convexity condition, we obtain the uniform estimates on the HJB equation for the $N$-particle system. Such estimates imply the displacement convexity/semi-concavity and thus the prior estimates on the solution to the HJB equation for generalized MFC problems. The global well-posedness of HJB/master equation for generalized MFC/potential MFGC is then proved thanks to the local well-posedness and the prior estimates. In view of the nature of the displacement convexity condition, such well-posedness is also true for the degenerated case. Our analysis on the $N$-particle system also induces an Lipschitz approximator to the optimal feedback function in generalized MFC/potential MFGC where an algebraic convergence rate is obtained. Furthermore, an alternative approximate Nash equilibrium is proposed based on the $N$-particle system, where the approximation error is quantified thanks to the aforementioned uniform estimates.
item.dc:creator: Huafu Liao, Chenchen Mou

item.title: Distributionally robust approximation property of neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2510.09177v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The universal approximation property uniformly with respect to weakly compact families of measures is established for several classes of neural networks. To that end, we prove that these neural networks are dense in Orlicz spaces, thereby extending classical universal approximation theorems even beyond the traditional $L^p$-setting. The covered classes of neural networks include widely used architectures like feedforward neural networks with non-polynomial activation functions, deep narrow networks with ReLU activation functions and functional input neural networks.
item.dc:creator: Mihriban Ceylan, David J. Pr\"omel

item.title: Consumption-Investment Problem in Rank-Based Models
item.description: arXiv:2510.20763v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a consumption-investment problem in a multi-asset market where the returns follow a generic rank-based model. Our main results are an HJB equation with Neumann boundary conditions for the value function, together with a corresponding verification theorem. The control problem is nonstandard due to the discontinuous nature of the coefficients in rank-based models, requiring a bespoke approach of independent mathematical interest. The special case of first-order models, prescribing constant drift and diffusion coefficients for the ranked returns, admits explicit solutions when the investor (a) is unconstrained, (b) abides by open market constraints or (c) is fully invested in the market. The explicit optimal strategies in all cases are related to the celebrated solution to Merton's problem, despite case (b) being intractable in the classic Merton setting.
item.dc:creator: David Itkin

item.title: Sampling Sphere Packings with Continuum Glauber Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2601.18748v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continuum Glauber dynamics is a spatial birth-death process whose stationary distribution is a Gibbs distribution. We establish a spectral gap for Continuum Glauber dynamics applied to Gibbs point processes with repulsive pair potentials, a well-known special case of which is the hard sphere model. For arbitrary-range repulsive pair potentials, we show that a continuous version of Spectral Independence suffices to establish a spectral gap. This extends the regime of activity for which Continuum Glauber dynamics is known to mix, yielding a simple efficient sampling algorithm for arbitrary-range pair potentials that matches the known efficient sampling regime for finite-range pair potentials currently based on specialized algorithms. As a consequence, we also improve the threshold up to which packings of fixed size/density can be efficiently sampled from a bounded domain, the first improvement since Kannan, Mahoney and Montenegro (2003). To prove these results, we develop continuous analogs of Spectral Independence and negative fields localization. We show that a stronger variant of zero-freeness implies Spectral Independence, which in turn allows us to run the localization scheme to boost the spectral gap of Continuum Glauber dynamics from smaller activity to larger activity. While this follows the high-level blueprint of Chen and Eldan (2022) for the discrete setting, we have to address several novel difficulties due to the continuous setting. Notably, we avoid discretization in the algorithm and the analysis and work directly in the continuous setting.
item.dc:creator: Aiya Kuchukova, Santosh S. Vempala, Daniel J. Zhang
